title.zh: 卷302 列傳八十九 徐本 汪由敦 汪承霈 来保 刘纶 刘跃雲 刘统勋 刘墉 刘镮之
title.en: Volume 302 Biographies 89: Xu Ben, Wang Youdun, Wang Chengpei, Lai Bao, Liu Lun, Liu Yueyun, Liu Tongxun, Liu Yong, Liu Huanzhi
title.raw: 卷302 列傳八十九 徐本 汪由敦 汪承霈 来保 刘纶 刘跃雲 刘统勋 刘墉 刘镮之

sentences.zh: 徐本汪由敦來保劉綸劉統勳

translations.literal: Xu Ben, Wang Youdun, Lai Bao, Liu Lun, Liu Tongxun
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ben, Wang Youdun, Lai Bao, Liu Lun, and Liu Tongxun

sentences.zh: 徐本，字立人，浙江錢塘人，尚書潮子。

translations.literal: Xu Ben, style name Liren, was a native of Qiantang in Zhejiang, son of Minister Xu Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ben, whose style name was Liren, came from Qiantang in Zhejiang and was the son of Minister Xu Chao.

sentences.zh: 本，康熙五十七年進士，改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: Ben passed the civil examinations in the fifty-seventh year of Kangxi, was made a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ben earned his jinshi degree in 1718, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and received appointment as a compiler.

sentences.zh: 雍正五年，提督貴州學政，授贊善，遷侍讀。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongzheng he was made educational commissioner of Guizhou with concurrent supervision, appointed reader-in-waiting, and promoted to reader.
translations.idiomatic: In 1727 he was appointed educational commissioner of Guizhou, then reader-in-waiting, and soon after promoted to reader.

sentences.zh: 七年，擢貴州按察使。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was promoted to surveillance commissioner of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1729 he was promoted to surveillance commissioner of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 八年，調江蘇，遷湖北布政使。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to Jiangsu and promoted to provincial treasurer of Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: In 1730 he was transferred to Jiangsu and then promoted to provincial treasurer of Hubei.

sentences.zh: 十年，擢安慶巡撫。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was promoted to governor of Anqing.
translations.idiomatic: In 1732 he was promoted to governor of Anqing.

sentences.zh: 奏定比緝盜賊章程，竊案責府州，盜案責臬司。

translations.literal: He memorialized to fix regulations for comparing and apprehending bandits: petty theft cases were the responsibility of prefectures and departments, robbery cases that of the provincial surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted regulations for tracking down bandits, assigning petty theft cases to prefectural authorities and robbery cases to the provincial surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 案多而未獲，巡撫親提。

translations.literal: When cases were numerous and culprits had not been caught, the governor personally conducted the inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: When many cases remained unsolved, the governor personally took charge of the investigations.

sentences.zh: 比立限，定勸懲。

translations.literal: He likewise set time limits and fixed rewards and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He also established deadlines and defined incentives and penalties.

sentences.zh: 上嘉之。

translations.literal: The emperor commended this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his work.

sentences.zh: 十一年，疏言：「雲、貴、廣西改流土司安置內地，例十人給官房五楹，地五十畝。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he memorialized: "For native chieftains in Yunnan, Guizhou, and Guangxi who were transformed and resettled in the interior, the rule is that ten persons receive five bays of official housing and fifty mu of land.
translations.idiomatic: In 1733 he memorialized: "When native chieftains from Yunnan, Guizhou, and Guangxi were brought under direct administration and resettled inland, the rule allotted five bays of official housing and fifty mu of land for every ten people.

sentences.zh: 安慶置二十一人，地遠在來安。

translations.literal: At Anqing twenty-one persons were settled, but the land lay far away in Lai'an.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-one such persons were settled at Anqing, but their allotted land lay far away in Lai'an.

sentences.zh: 請變價別購，俾耕以食。」

translations.literal: He requested that the property be sold and other land purchased so they could farm for their livelihood."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that the distant plots be sold and other land bought nearby so they could farm for their sustenance."

sentences.zh: 又疏言：「州縣徵糧，例由府道封櫃，請改州縣自封。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "When prefectures and districts collected grain taxes, by rule the prefectural and circuit offices sealed the coffers; he requested that districts and counties seal them themselves.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed: "Grain tax collection, which customarily required sealing by prefectural and circuit offices, should be changed so that counties and districts sealed the funds themselves.

sentences.zh: 完糧十截串票改仍用三連由票，零戶銀以下以十錢當一分。」

translations.literal: The ten-section tax receipt for completed payments was changed back to the three-part tax warrant, and for fractional household payments amounts below one fen were reckoned with ten cash as one fen."
translations.idiomatic: He restored the three-part tax warrant in place of the ten-section receipt for completed payments, and set ten cash equal to one fen for fractional household payments."

sentences.zh: 又疏言：「壽州濱淮，盜聚族而居，假捕魚為業，每出劫掠，已次第捕治，令漁船編甲。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Shouzhou lies along the Huai River, where bandits live in clan settlements and pretend to fish for a living, going out to plunder whenever they can; they have been captured and punished in turn, and fishing boats are now registered in militia units.
translations.idiomatic: He further reported: "Along the Huai at Shouzhou, bandit clans posing as fishermen had been raiding in turn; after successive arrests, fishing boats were now organized into militia units.

sentences.zh: 孫、平、焦、鄧諸姓設族正，有盜不時舉發。」

translations.literal: Clan heads were appointed among the Sun, Ping, Jiao, and Deng surnames, who were to report any theft without delay."
translations.idiomatic: Clan heads were appointed among the Sun, Ping, Jiao, and Deng families to report banditry promptly."

sentences.zh: 皆下部議行。

translations.literal: All were referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: All these proposals were sent to the ministries for deliberation and enactment.

sentences.zh: 召授左都御史。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed left censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital and appointed left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 十二年，遷工部尚書、協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was transferred to minister of works and made associate grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In 1734 he was made minister of works and associate grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 浙江衢州民王益善邪教惑眾，命本會總督程元章按治，請改設衢州總兵、金衢嚴巡道以下官，並更定營製，下部議行。

translations.literal: Wang Yishan of Quzhou in Zhejiang deluded the people with heterodox teachings; Ben was ordered to join Governor-General Cheng Yuanzhang in investigating, and requested the establishment of a Quzhou regional commander and officials down to the Jinhua-Quzhou-Yanzhou circuit intendant, with camp organization revised; this was referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Yishan of Quzhou, Zhejiang, led a heterodox sect that misled the populace, Xu Ben was ordered to join Governor-General Cheng Yuanzhang in suppressing it. He proposed creating a Quzhou regional commander and revising posts through the Jinhua-Quzhou-Yanzhou circuit intendant, along with reorganizing the garrison; the proposal was sent to the ministries for approval.

sentences.zh: 十三年五月，命同寶親王，果親王，大學士鄂爾泰、張廷玉等辦理苗疆事務。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the thirteenth year he was ordered, together with Prince Bao, Prince Guo, and Grand Secretaries Ortai and Zhang Tingyu, to handle Miao frontier affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of 1735 he was ordered, together with Princes Bao and Guo and Grand Secretaries Ortai and Zhang Tingyu, to manage affairs on the Miao frontier.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，命在辦理軍機處行走，調刑部尚書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong acceded, he was ordered to serve in the Grand Council and was transferred to minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qianlong Emperor took the throne, Xu Ben was assigned to the Grand Council and transferred to minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 尋命協辦總理事務。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was ordered to assist in general affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to assist in managing general state affairs.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，授東閣大學士兼禮部尚書，充世宗實錄總裁。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong he was made grand secretary of the Eastern Pavilion and concurrent minister of rites, and served as chief compiler of the Veritable Records of Emperor Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: In 1736 he was appointed grand secretary of the Eastern Pavilion and concurrent minister of rites, and named chief compiler of the Veritable Records of the Yongzheng Emperor.

sentences.zh: 二年，直南書房。

translations.literal: In the second year he served in the Southern Study.
translations.idiomatic: In 1737 he was assigned to the Southern Study.

sentences.zh: 以協辦總理事務，予拖沙喇哈番世職。

translations.literal: For assisting in general affairs of state he was granted the hereditary rank of Dashala ha.
translations.idiomatic: For his service assisting in general state affairs, he was granted the hereditary rank of Dashala ha.

sentences.zh: 三年，授辦理軍機大臣。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1738 he was appointed a Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 四年，加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was given the additional title of Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In 1739 he received the additional title Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 七年，兼管戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was given concurrent charge of the ministry of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In 1742 he was given concurrent charge as minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 九年六月，以病乞休，加太子太傅致仕。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the ninth year, citing illness he requested retirement and was given the additional title of Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and allowed to retire.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of 1744 he retired on grounds of illness, receiving the additional title Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 遣御前侍衛永興齎賜御用衣冠、內府文綺貂皮，上親臨其第慰問賜詩。

translations.literal: The imperial bodyguard Yongxing was sent bearing gifts of imperial robes, palace silks, and sable fur; the emperor personally visited his residence to console him and bestowed a poem.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent the imperial bodyguard Yongxing with robes, palace silks, and sable fur, then visited Xu Ben's home in person to console him and presented a poem.

sentences.zh: 命其子侍講學士​​以烜送歸里，在籍食俸。

translations.literal: His son, reader-in-waiting Xu Yixuan, was ordered to escort him home, where he received his salary while remaining on the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: His son, reader-in-waiting Xu Yixuan, was ordered to escort him home, where he continued to draw his salary while on leave in his native place.

sentences.zh: 明年，上念本歸將一載，复賜詩。

translations.literal: The next year, as the emperor reflected that Ben had been home nearly a year, he again bestowed a poem.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, mindful that nearly a year had passed since Xu Ben's return home, the emperor bestowed another poem.

sentences.zh: 十二年，本卒，加少傅，發白金千治喪。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Ben died; he was given the posthumous title of Junior Preceptor and a thousand taels of silver for funeral expenses.
translations.idiomatic: In 1747 Xu Ben died; he was posthumously given the title Junior Preceptor and a thousand taels of silver for funeral expenses.

sentences.zh: 浙江巡撫顧琮往祭，諡文穆。

translations.literal: Zhejiang Governor Gu Cong went to perform the sacrifice, and the posthumous name Wenmu was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: Zhejiang Governor Gu Cong conducted the memorial rites, and Xu Ben was given the posthumous name Wenmu.

sentences.zh: 上南巡，所經郡縣遣祭舊臣，禮部奏請未及本，上特命遣祭。

translations.literal: On the emperor's southern tour, each prefecture and district he passed was ordered to sacrifice to former ministers; the ministry of rites had not yet included Ben in its memorial, so the emperor specially ordered sacrifices sent.
translations.idiomatic: During the emperor's southern tour, each locality he passed was to offer sacrifices to former ministers, but the ministry of rites had not yet listed Xu Ben; the emperor specially ordered rites performed for him.

sentences.zh: 祀京師賢良祠。

translations.literal: He was enshrined in the Shrine of Worthies in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was enshrined in the capital's Shrine of Worthies.

sentences.zh: 以烜，進士，官至禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: Yixuan was a jinshi and rose to vice minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yixuan was a jinshi who rose to vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 汪由敦，字師茗，浙江錢塘人，原籍安徽休寧。

translations.literal: Wang Youdun, style name Shiming, was a native of Qiantang in Zhejiang, with original domicile in Xiuning, Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Youdun, whose style name was Shiming, came from Qiantang in Zhejiang, though his ancestral home was Xiuning in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 雍正二年進士，選庶吉士。

translations.literal: He passed the civil examinations in the second year of Yongzheng and was selected as a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in 1724 and was selected as a Hanlin bachelor.

sentences.zh: 遭父喪，以篡修明史，命在館守制。

translations.literal: When his father died, because he was engaged in compiling the History of Ming, he was ordered to observe mourning while remaining at the academy.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, he was ordered to remain at the academy observing mourning while continuing work on the History of Ming.

sentences.zh: 喪終，三遷內閣​​學士，直上書房。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was promoted three times to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat and served in the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he was promoted three times to grand secretary and assigned to the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二年，廷臣妄傳除目，為言官執奏，語連由敦，未得旨，由敦具疏辨。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianlong court officials falsely spread word of appointments; censors memorialized on it, and the matter touched Youdun; as no edict had issued, Youdun submitted a memorial in his defense.
translations.idiomatic: In 1737 court officials falsely circulated word of impending appointments; censors reported it, implicating Youdun, who had received no edict and submitted a memorial in his own defense.

sentences.zh: 上詰由敦何以先知，足見有為之耳目者，其人必不謹。

translations.literal: The emperor questioned how Youdun knew beforehand, showing clearly that someone was acting as his informant, and such a person must be careless.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor demanded to know how Youdun had known in advance, concluding that someone must have been leaking information to him and that such conduct was inexcusably careless.

sentences.zh: 左授侍讀學士。

translations.literal: He was demoted to reader-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 累遷工部尚書，調刑部，兼署左都御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to minister of works, transferred to the ministry of justice, and given acting charge as left censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to minister of works, was transferred to the ministry of justice, and served concurrently as acting left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 十一年，命在軍機處行走。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was ordered to serve in the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: In 1746 he was assigned to the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 十四年，金川平，加太子少師。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year the Jinchuan campaign was pacified and he was given the additional title of Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In 1749, after the pacification of Jinchuan, he received the additional title Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 是歲命協辦大學士。

translations.literal: That year he was ordered to serve as associate grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he was made associate grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 由敦出大學士張廷玉門，其直軍機處，廷玉薦也。

translations.literal: Youdun had come from the school of Grand Secretary Zhang Tingyu, and his assignment to the Grand Council was Zhang's recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: Youdun had been a protégé of Grand Secretary Zhang Tingyu, who recommended him for the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 時軍機處諸大臣，鄂爾泰已卒，廷玉為班首，而訥親被上眷，日入承旨，出令由敦屬草，慮不當上意，輒令易稿，至三四不已，傅恆為不平。

translations.literal: At that time among the Grand Councilors Ortai had already died and Zhang Tingyu was senior, but Ne Qin enjoyed the emperor's favor, entering daily to receive instructions; when edicts went out he ordered Youdun to draft them, and fearing they might not suit the emperor's intent would have drafts changed again and again, even three or four times without stopping; Fu Heng was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Ortai had died and Zhang Tingyu led the council, but Ne Qin, favored by the emperor, received instructions daily and had Youdun draft edicts, repeatedly ordering revisions—sometimes three or four times—lest they miss the emperor's intent; Fu Heng resented this.

sentences.zh: 及訥親誅，傅恆自金川還朝，引諸大臣共承旨以為常。

translations.literal: After Ne Qin was executed, Fu Heng returned from Jinchuan to court and led the grand ministers to receive instructions jointly as the regular practice.
translations.idiomatic: After Ne Qin's execution, Fu Heng returned from Jinchuan and established the practice of councilors receiving instructions together.

sentences.zh: 廷玉致仕將歸，以世宗遺詔許配享太廟，乞上一言為券，謝恩未親至。

translations.literal: As Zhang Tingyu was retiring and about to return home, relying on Emperor Shizong's testamentary edict permitting him posthumous enshrinement in the Imperial Ancestral Temple, he begged the emperor for a confirming word as warrant; he did not come in person to give thanks.
translations.idiomatic: As Zhang Tingyu prepared to retire, he cited the Yongzheng Emperor's testament allowing him posthumous enshrinement in the Imperial Ancestral Temple and asked for a confirming edict, but failed to appear in person to give thanks.

sentences.zh: 傳旨詰責，傅恆與由敦承旨，由敦免冠叩首，言廷玉蒙恩體恤，乞終始矜全，若明旨詰責，則廷玉罪無可逭。

translations.literal: An edict was transmitted rebuking him; Fu Heng and Youdun received the instruction, and Youdun removed his hat and kowtowed, saying Zhang Tingyu had received the emperor's gracious consideration and begging that he be shown forbearance to the end; if an explicit edict of rebuke issued, Zhang Tingyu's offense would admit no escape.
translations.idiomatic: A rebuking edict was issued; Fu Heng and Youdun received it, and Youdun kowtowed bareheaded, pleading that Zhang Tingyu had enjoyed the emperor's gracious favor and begging mercy throughout; an explicit rebuke, he said, would leave Zhang Tingyu with no defense.

sentences.zh: 次日，廷玉早入朝，上責由敦漏言，徇師生私恩，不顧公議。

translations.literal: The next day Zhang Tingyu entered court early; the emperor rebuked Youdun for leaking word, indulging private teacher-student favor and disregarding public opinion.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Zhang Tingyu came to court early; the emperor rebuked Youdun for leaking the edict, putting private loyalty to his teacher ahead of public duty.

sentences.zh: 解協辦大學士，並罷尚書，仍在尚書任贖罪。

translations.literal: He was removed as associate grand secretary and dismissed as minister, yet remained at his ministerial post to atone for his offense.
translations.idiomatic: He was stripped of his associate grand secretary title and ministerial rank, yet kept at his ministerial post to atone for the offense.

sentences.zh: 十五年，命復任。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was ordered to resume his duties.
translations.idiomatic: In 1750 he was ordered to resume his posts.

sentences.zh: 上閱永定河工，令由敦同大學士傅恆、總督方觀承會勘南岸建壩，請於張仙務、雙營葺舊壩二，馬家鋪及冰窖以東增新壩亦二，如所議。

translations.literal: The emperor inspected works on the Yongding River and ordered Youdun, together with Grand Secretary Fu Heng and Governor-General Fang Guancheng, to survey jointly the construction of dikes on the south bank; they requested repairing two old dikes at Zhangxianwu and Shuangying and building two new dikes east of Majiapu and Bingjiao, which was approved as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: While inspecting Yongding River works, the emperor sent Youdun with Grand Secretary Fu Heng and Governor-General Fang Guancheng to survey south-bank dike construction. They proposed repairing two old dikes at Zhangxianwu and Shuangying and building two new ones east of Majiapu and Bingjiao, which was approved.

sentences.zh: 四川學政硃荃以匿喪黷賄得罪，由敦所薦舉，吏議奪職。

translations.literal: Zhu Quan, educational commissioner of Sichuan, was punished for concealing mourning and accepting bribes; he had been recommended by Youdun, and the personnel office proposed stripping Youdun of his post.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quan, educational commissioner of Sichuan, was punished for concealing mourning and taking bribes; as Youdun had recommended him, the personnel office proposed stripping Youdun of office.

sentences.zh: 上以由敦謹慎，長於學問，命降授兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: Because the emperor considered Youdun careful and accomplished in scholarship, he ordered him demoted to vice minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: Considering Youdun careful and learned, the emperor merely demoted him to vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 俄，永定河堤決，復命赴固安監塞口。

translations.literal: Soon the Yongding River dike burst, and he was again ordered to go to Gu'an to supervise closing the breach.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Yongding dike burst, and he was again sent to Gu'an to supervise closing the breach.

sentences.zh: 有請別開新河者，由敦主仍濬舊河，亦如所議。

translations.literal: Some proposed cutting a new channel, but Youdun advocated dredging the old river, which was likewise approved.
translations.idiomatic: When some proposed cutting a new channel, Youdun argued for dredging the old river, and this too was approved.

sentences.zh: 十六年，調戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was transferred to vice minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In 1751 he was transferred to vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 命同大學士高斌勘天津等處河工，請濬永定河下流，疏王慶坨引河，增鳳河堤壩，培東岸堤障東淀。

translations.literal: He was ordered, together with Grand Secretary Gao Bin, to survey river works at Tianjin and elsewhere; they requested dredging the lower Yongding River, clearing the Wangqingtuo diversion canal, strengthening dikes and dams on the Feng River, and raising the east-bank dike to shield the Eastern Marshes.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered with Grand Secretary Gao Bin to survey river works around Tianjin, they proposed dredging the lower Yongding, clearing the Wangqingtuo diversion, strengthening Feng River dikes, and raising the east bank to protect the Eastern Marshes.

sentences.zh: 十七年，授工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was appointed minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: In 1752 he was appointed minister of works.

sentences.zh: 十九年，加太子太傅，兼刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was given the additional title of Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and concurrent charge as minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: In 1754 he received the additional title Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and concurrent appointment as minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 二十年，準噶爾平，軍機大臣得議敘。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year Dzungaria was pacified and Grand Councilors were eligible for merit review.
translations.idiomatic: In 1755, after the pacification of Dzungaria, Grand Councilors became eligible for merit review.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，調工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was transferred to minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: In 1756 he was transferred to minister of works.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，授吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was appointed minister of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In 1757 he was appointed minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，卒，上親臨賜奠，贈太子太師，諡文端。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he died; the emperor personally came to bestow funeral offerings, posthumously granted him the title of Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, and conferred the posthumous name Wenduan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1758 he died; the emperor came in person to offer funeral rites, posthumously granted him Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, and gave him the posthumous name Wenduan.

sentences.zh: 由敦篤內行，記誦尤淹博，文章典重有體。

translations.literal: Youdun was sincere in personal conduct, especially broad in memory and learning, and his writings were classical, weighty, and well formed.
translations.idiomatic: Youdun was known for personal integrity, exceptional erudition and memory, and writing that was dignified and well structured.

sentences.zh: 內直幾三十年，以恭謹受上知。

translations.literal: He served in the inner palace for nearly thirty years and won the emperor's trust through respectful care.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the inner palace for nearly thirty years and won the emperor's trust through respectful diligence.

sentences.zh: 乾隆間，大臣初入直軍機處，上以日所製詩用丹筆作草，或口授令移錄，謂之「詩片」。

translations.literal: During the Qianlong reign, when a minister first entered service in the Grand Council, the emperor would use cinnabar brush to draft in cursive the poems he composed each day, or dictate them for transcription, calling these "poem slips."
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianlong reign, new Grand Councilors first copied the emperor's daily poems—drafted in cinnabar brush or dictated for transcription—in exercises called "poem slips."

sentences.zh: 久無誤，乃使撰擬諭旨。

translations.literal: Only after long service without error was he allowed to draft edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Only after long service without error were they entrusted to draft edicts.

sentences.zh: 由敦能彊識，當上意。

translations.literal: Youdun had a powerful memory and suited the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Youdun's exceptional memory suited the emperor's expectations.

sentences.zh: 上出謁陵及巡幸必從，入承旨，耳受心識，出即傳寫，不遺一字。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor went to pay respects at the tombs or on tour, Youdun accompanied him; entering to receive instructions, he heard with his ears and retained them in his mind, and on coming out immediately transcribed them without omitting a single character.
translations.idiomatic: He always accompanied the emperor on tomb visits and tours, received instructions by ear, memorized them, and transcribed them afterward without omitting a word.

sentences.zh: 其卒也，諭稱其「老誠端恪，敏慎安詳，學問淵深，文辭雅正」，並賦詩悼之。

translations.literal: At his death an edict praised him as "aged in sincerity, upright and respectful, keen yet calm and thorough, deep in learning, elegant and correct in literary style," and the emperor also composed an elegiac poem.
translations.idiomatic: At his death an edict praised him as "sincere and upright in old age, keen yet calm and thorough, deep in learning, elegant in literary style," and the emperor composed an elegy.

sentences.zh: 又以由敦善書，命館臣排次上石，曰時晴齋法帖。

translations.literal: Because Youdun excelled at calligraphy, academicians were ordered to arrange his works for carving on stone, titled the Shiqing Studio Model Calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: As Youdun was also celebrated for calligraphy, academicians arranged his works for stone engraving as the Shiqing Studio Model Calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 上賦懷舊詩，列五詞臣中，稱其書比張照云雲。

translations.literal: The emperor composed a nostalgic poem, ranking him among five literary ministers and comparing his calligraphy to Zhang Zhao's, and so forth.
translations.idiomatic: In a nostalgic poem the emperor ranked him among five leading literary ministers and compared his calligraphy to Zhang Zhao's.

sentences.zh: 子承沆、承霈、承𩆩。

translations.literal: His sons were Chenghang, Chengpei, and Cheng Hao.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Chenghang, Chengpei, and Cheng Hao.

sentences.zh: 承霈，字春農。

translations.literal: Chengpei, style name Chunnong.
translations.idiomatic: Chengpei, whose style name was Chunnong.

sentences.zh: 由敦既卒，喪終，承霈以賜祭葬入謝。

translations.literal: After Youdun died and mourning ended, Chengpei entered court to give thanks for the bestowed sacrificial and funeral rites.
translations.idiomatic: After Youdun's death, when mourning ended Chengpei came to court to thank the emperor for the granted funeral rites.

sentences.zh: 傅恆為言承霈書類由敦，授兵部主事，充軍機處章京。

translations.literal: Fu Heng spoke on his behalf, saying Chengpei's calligraphy resembled Youdun's; he was appointed a secretary in the ministry of war and served as a Grand Council clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Heng remarked that Chengpei's calligraphy resembled his father's; he was appointed a secretary in the ministry of war and assigned as a Grand Council clerk.

sentences.zh: 累遷郎中，除福建邵武知府。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to director and appointed prefect of Shaowu in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to director and was appointed prefect of Shaowu in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 時母年八十，請軍機大臣為陳情，留京供職，复補戶部郎中。

translations.literal: At the time his mother was eighty; he asked the Grand Councilors to plead his case and was kept in the capital on duty, then reappointed as a director in the ministry of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was then eighty; he asked the Grand Councilors to intercede and was kept at a post in the capital, later reappointed as a director in the ministry of revenue.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，師討小金川，上命戶部侍郎桂林出督餉，以承霈從。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year the army campaigned against Lesser Jinchuan; the emperor ordered Vice Minister of Revenue Guilin to go out and supervise supplies, with Chengpei accompanying him.
translations.idiomatic: In 1771, during the campaign against Lesser Jinchuan, the emperor sent Vice Minister Guilin to supervise supplies, with Chengpei accompanying him.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，阿爾泰、宋元俊劾桂林以金與土酋贖所掠軍士，辭連承霈，命逮治。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year Altai and Song Yuanjun impeached Guilin for giving gold to native chieftains to ransom captured soldiers, implicating Chengpei in the charge; he was ordered arrested and tried.
translations.idiomatic: In 1772 Altai and Song Yuanjun impeached Guilin for paying native chieftains gold to ransom captured soldiers, implicating Chengpei; he was ordered arrested.

sentences.zh: 俄，事白，仍以郎中充軍機處章京。

translations.literal: Soon the matter was cleared and he again served as a director and Grand Council clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was cleared and restored as a director and Grand Council clerk.

sentences.zh: 累遷工部右侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to right vice minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to right vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 甘肅冒賑事發，部議凡在甘肅納捐監生，應禁革毋許應試，及自別途出身。

translations.literal: When the Gansu relief-fund fraud case broke, the ministry proposed that all students who had purchased offices through donations in Gansu should be barred from examinations and from advancement by other routes.
translations.idiomatic: When the Gansu relief-fund fraud scandal broke, the ministry proposed barring all donation-purchased students in Gansu from examinations and alternate routes to office.

sentences.zh: 承霈奏人數甚多，乞開自新之路，令納金如例，許考試及自別途出身，得旨俞允。

translations.literal: Chengpei memorialized that the number of persons was very large and begged to open a path of renewal, allowing payment of gold as usual so they might take examinations and advance by other routes; an edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: Chengpei noted the large number affected and asked that they be allowed to pay fines as usual and resume examinations and alternate advancement; the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 四十年，上校射，承霈連發中的，賞花翎。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year, at the emperor's archery review, Chengpei hit the target repeatedly in succession and was rewarded with a peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In 1775, at the imperial archery review, Chengpei hit the target repeatedly and was rewarded with a peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 調戶部右侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to right vice minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to right vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 五十四年，坐監臨順天鄉試失察，左遷通政使。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year, for failure to detect misconduct while supervising the Shuntian provincial examination, he was demoted to commissioner of the Court of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: In 1789, for failing to detect misconduct while supervising the Shuntian provincial examination, he was demoted to commissioner of the Court of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 累遷復至侍郎。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he again reached vice minister.
translations.idiomatic: Through successive promotions he again rose to vice minister.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶五年，授左都御史，遷兵部尚書，兼領順天府尹。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jiaqing he was appointed left censor-in-chief, transferred to minister of war, and given concurrent charge as Shuntian metropolitan magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: In 1800 he was appointed left censor-in-chief, then minister of war, with concurrent charge as Shuntian metropolitan magistrate.

sentences.zh: 六年，永定河水溢，上命治賑，得旨獎敘。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the Yongding River overflowed; the emperor ordered relief work, and he received an edict of commendation for merit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1801, when the Yongding overflowed, the emperor ordered relief efforts and commended his service.

sentences.zh: 七年，上將幸木蘭，承霈請罷停圍，不許。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, as the emperor was about to visit Mulan, Chengpei requested suspension of the hunting enclosure; this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: In 1802, as the emperor prepared to visit Mulan, Chengpei asked to suspend the autumn hunt enclosure; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 尋改左都御史，署兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to left censor-in-chief and given acting charge as minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made left censor-in-chief with acting charge as minister of war.

sentences.zh: 北城盜發，上責承霈不稱職，以二品冠服致仕。

translations.literal: When bandits broke out in the northern city, the emperor blamed Chengpei for incompetence and allowed him to retire wearing second-rank cap and robe.
translations.idiomatic: After bandits raided the northern city, the emperor blamed Chengpei for incompetence and let him retire with second-rank honors.

sentences.zh: 十年，卒，詔視尚書例議卹。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he died; an edict ordered funeral benefits deliberated according to the precedent for ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In 1805 he died; an edict ordered funeral benefits according to ministerial precedent.

sentences.zh: 來保，字學圃，喜塔臘氏，滿洲正白旗人。

translations.literal: Lai Bao, style name Xuepu, of the Xitala clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Bao, whose style name was Xuepu, of the Xitala clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 初隸內務府。

translations.literal: He was first attached to the Imperial Household Department.
translations.idiomatic: He began in the Imperial Household Department.

sentences.zh: 康熙中，自庫使授侍衛，再奪職。

translations.literal: During the Kangxi reign he rose from a storehouse clerk to bodyguard, and twice had his post stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kangxi he rose from storehouse clerk to bodyguard and twice lost his post.

sentences.zh: 五十七年，复授三等侍衛。

translations.literal: In the fifty-seventh year he was again appointed a third-rank bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: In 1718 he was again appointed a third-rank bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 雍正初，擢內務府總管。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongzheng he was promoted to superintendent of the Imperial Household Department.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongzheng reign he became superintendent of the Imperial Household Department.

sentences.zh: 坐內務府披甲裁額，眾閧廉親王允禩第，來保等奏不實，复奪職。

translations.literal: For the Household Department's reduction of armor quotas, when a crowd stormed Prince Lian Yunsi's residence, Lai Bao and others memorialized inaccurately, and he again lost his post.
translations.idiomatic: When armor quotas were cut and a mob stormed Prince Lian Yunsi's residence, Lai Bao and others filed an inaccurate report and he again lost his post.

sentences.zh: 起景陵掌關防郎中，再遷復為內務府總管，署工部尚書。

translations.literal: He was reappointed director of the Jingling seal office, then promoted again to superintendent of the Imperial Household Department and given acting charge as minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: He was reappointed director of the Jingling seal office, then again made Household superintendent with acting charge as minister of works.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「滿洲騎射較優，沿邊古北口諸處提鎮以下，請兼用滿洲，資控制。」

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Manchu horsemanship and archery are comparatively superior; along the frontier at Gubeikou and elsewhere, from regional commanders downward, he requested that Manchus be employed concurrently to aid control."
translations.idiomatic: He proposed that because Manchu horsemanship and archery were superior, regional commanders along the frontier at Gubeikou and elsewhere should include Manchu officers to strengthen control."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年十二月，大學士管浙江總督嵇曾筠、江蘇巡撫邵基疏請停辦戊午銅運，下部議。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Qianlong, Grand Secretary and acting Zhejiang Governor-General Ji Zengjun and Jiangsu Governor Shao Ji memorialized requesting suspension of the wuwu-year copper transport; the matter was referred to the ministries for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of 1736, Grand Secretary and acting Zhejiang Governor-General Ji Zengjun and Jiangsu Governor Shao Ji asked to suspend the wuwu-year copper transport; the matter went to the ministries.

sentences.zh: 來保奏：「積欠數盈六百萬，應停辦一年，以清舊款。

translations.literal: Lai Bao memorialized: "Arrears exceed six million; transport should be suspended for one year to clear old accounts.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Bao reported: "Arrears exceed six million; transport should be suspended for one year to clear old accounts.

sentences.zh: 但己未以後，仍招商採買，行之數年，積欠復多，又當停辦。

translations.literal: But after the jiwei year merchants were still invited to purchase on contract; after several years arrears again grew large, and suspension should again be ordered.
translations.idiomatic: After the jiwei year, however, contracted merchant purchases had resumed; within a few years arrears mounted again, warranting another suspension.

sentences.zh: 請敕部並下各直省督撫曉諭，聽商具貲本出洋採買，不必先給價值，隨到即收，不拘多寡，但不得剋扣抑勒，重滋商累。」

translations.literal: He requested that the ministries be ordered and governors-general and governors of all provinces instructed, allowing merchants to supply capital and go abroad to purchase, without advance payment required; upon arrival goods would be accepted regardless of quantity, but deductions and coercion must not be imposed to burden merchants further."
translations.idiomatic: He asked the ministries and all provincial governors to inform merchants they might supply their own capital for overseas purchases without advance payment, accepting goods upon arrival in any quantity, but forbidding deductions or coercion that would burden them further."

sentences.zh: 總理王大臣議覆允行。

translations.literal: The prince-ministers in charge deliberated and approved implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising prince-ministers approved the plan.

sentences.zh: 二年六月，上以運河水淺，糧船至臨清以北，尤多阻滯，由於衛河上游各渠口居民私洩過多。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year the emperor noted that canal water was shallow and grain transports north of Linqing were especially obstructed, owing to excessive private diversion by residents at the various canal mouths upstream on the Wei River.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of 1737 the emperor noted shallow canal waters and severe delays for grain boats north of Linqing, caused by excessive private diversion at Wei River canal mouths upstream.

sentences.zh: 敕直隸、河南督撫等照前河臣靳輔題准定例，稽查嚴禁。

translations.literal: He ordered the governors-general and governors of Zhili and Henan and others to follow the approved regulations formerly submitted by river official Jin Fu, conducting strict inspection and prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Zhili and Henan authorities to enforce the regulations once approved by the river official Jin Fu through strict inspection.

sentences.zh: 來保奏言：「水淺運阻，查禁不得不嚴。

translations.literal: Lai Bao memorialized: "With shallow water and transport obstruction, prohibition and inspection cannot but be strict.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Bao replied: "With shallow water and transport obstruction, strict enforcement cannot be avoided.

sentences.zh: 但衛水發源河南，至臨清五百餘裡。

translations.literal: But the Wei River rises in Henan and extends more than five hundred li to Linqing.
translations.idiomatic: But the Wei River rises in Henan and runs more than five hundred li to Linqing.

sentences.zh: 沿河居民不知幾千萬家，待溉之地不知幾千百頃。

translations.literal: Along the river residents number tens of millions of households, and land awaiting irrigation amounts to thousands upon thousands of qing.
translations.idiomatic: Millions of households line its banks, and thousands of qing await irrigation.

sentences.zh: 今秋成在望，已非灌溉之期，所慮者有司奉行過當。

translations.literal: Now the autumn harvest is in sight and it is no longer the season for irrigation; what is feared is that officials may enforce the rules excessively.
translations.idiomatic: With harvest near and irrigation season past, he feared officials might enforce the rules excessively.

sentences.zh: 後雖運河未至淺阻，而一入五月，渠口盡行堵塞，坐使​​有用之利置之無用，恐不無廢時失業者，不稱仁育萬民之意。

translations.literal: Later, even when the canal has not become shallow and obstructed, once the fifth month arrives all canal mouths are entirely blocked, leaving useful benefits unused; there will likely be those who lose their season and livelihood, which does not accord with the intent of nurturing all people benevolently.
translations.idiomatic: Even when the canal was not shallow, blocking every outlet from the fifth month onward would waste irrigation and leave farmers idle—contrary to the emperor's intent to nurture the people.

sentences.zh: 當使漕運不致淺阻，民田亦得灌溉，或暫禁於淺阻之年，而不禁於深通之歲。

translations.literal: Transport should not be made shallow and obstructed, yet civilian fields should also receive irrigation; prohibition might be temporary in years of shallow obstruction but not in years when the channel runs deep and clear.
translations.idiomatic: Grain transport and field irrigation should both be served—temporary bans in shallow years, but not when the channel ran deep.

sentences.zh: 應令督撫、河道諸臣悉心調劑，以期兩便。」

translations.literal: Governors-general, governors, and river officials should be ordered to adjust matters attentively, seeking convenience for both."
translations.idiomatic: Governors and river officials should balance both needs carefully."

sentences.zh: 疏入，上命侍郎趙殿最、侍衛安寧會同督撫查勘，請於漕船將抵臨清，視運河水盈縮，定渠閘啟閉。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the emperor ordered Vice Minister Zhao Dianzui and bodyguard Anning to join governors-general and governors in surveying; they requested that when grain boats were about to reach Linqing, sluice gates be opened or closed according to whether Grand Canal water was full or low.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Vice Minister Zhao Dianzui and bodyguard Anning to survey with provincial authorities, proposing that sluice gates be opened or closed as grain boats neared Linqing according to canal water levels.

sentences.zh: 十二月，授工部尚書，兼議政大臣。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he was appointed minister of works and made a deliberative minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he was appointed minister of works and deliberative minister.

sentences.zh: 四年，病，請解任，上不許。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, ill, he requested to be relieved of office; the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: In 1739, ill, he asked to resign; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 十二月，授內大臣，賜紫禁城內騎馬。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he was appointed inner minister and granted the privilege of riding within the Forbidden City.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he became an inner minister and was granted the privilege of riding inside the Forbidden City.

sentences.zh: 五年，調刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: In 1740 he was transferred to minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 上以來保奉職勤，命改隸正白旗滿洲，所立佐領準世襲。

translations.literal: Because the emperor considered Lai Bao diligent in office, he ordered him transferred to the Manchu Plain White Banner, and the assistant commandership he established was approved as hereditary.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Lai Bao diligent, the emperor transferred him to the Manchu Plain White Banner and made his assistant commandership hereditary.

sentences.zh: 六月，御史沈世楓奏來保誠愨有餘，習練不足，不勝刑部繁要之任。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Censor Shen Shifeng memorialized that Lai Bao had sincerity in excess but insufficient practical experience and could not bear the heavy and demanding duties of the ministry of justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Censor Shen Shifeng reported that Lai Bao was sincere but inexperienced and unfit for the demanding ministry of justice.

sentences.zh: 諭曰：「來保人實可信，然世楓所言，頗中其病。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Lai Bao is in truth trustworthy, yet what Shifeng said hits his weakness fairly well.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Lai Bao is trustworthy, yet Shen Shifeng's criticism hits the mark.

sentences.zh: 儻因此自知省惕，則心志虛公，而才識亦將日進。

translations.literal: If through this he comes to know himself and grow cautious, his mind will be open and impartial, and his talent and insight will also advance day by day.
translations.idiomatic: If he takes this to heart, his mind will grow more impartial and his abilities will improve daily.

sentences.zh: 此聞過而喜，所以稱賢也。」

translations.literal: To hear one's faults and rejoice in it is what is called worthiness."
translations.idiomatic: Delighting in criticism is the mark of a worthy man."

sentences.zh: 九年，命如奉天按將軍額洛圖侵餉納賄狀，論如律。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was ordered to try according to law the case of Fengtian investigating general Eluotu, who had embezzled rations and accepted bribes.
translations.idiomatic: In 1744 he was ordered to try Fengtian investigating general Eluotu for embezzling rations and taking bribes according to law.

sentences.zh: 十年，調禮部尚書，加太子太保，授領侍衛內大臣。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to minister of rites, given the additional title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and appointed leading bodyguard inner minister.
translations.idiomatic: In 1745 he was made minister of rites, Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and leading bodyguard inner minister.

sentences.zh: 尋授吏部尚書，協辦大學士。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed minister of personnel and associate grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed minister of personnel and associate grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 十二月，授武英殿大學士。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he was appointed grand secretary of the Hall of Military Glory.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he was appointed grand secretary of the Hall of Military Glory.

sentences.zh: 十三年九月，命為軍機大臣。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the thirteenth year he was appointed Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of 1748 he was appointed Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 十四年，金川凱旋，進太子太傅，兼管兵部、刑部事。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, with triumphant return from Jinchuan, he was advanced to Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and given concurrent charge of the ministries of war and justice.
translations.idiomatic: In 1749, after the Jinchuan victory, he was promoted to Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent with concurrent charge of the ministries of war and justice.

sentences.zh: 十五年三月，來保年七十，上製詩賚之。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifteenth year, when Lai Bao reached seventy, the emperor composed a poem and bestowed it on him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of 1750, when Lai Bao turned seventy, the emperor composed and bestowed a congratulatory poem.

sentences.zh: 十六年，兼管吏部事。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was given concurrent charge of the ministry of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In 1751 he was given concurrent charge of the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，來保年八十，复賜御製詩。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, when Lai Bao reached eighty, the emperor again bestowed an imperial poem.
translations.idiomatic: In 1760, when Lai Bao turned eighty, the emperor again bestowed an imperial poem.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，兼管禮部事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was given concurrent charge of the ministry of rites.
translations.idiomatic: In 1761 he was given concurrent charge of the ministry of rites.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，卒，年八十四，贈太保，祀賢良祠，諡文端。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he died at the age of eighty-four; he was posthumously granted the title of Grand Guardian and enshrined in the Shrine of Worthies, with the posthumous name Wenduan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1764 he died at eighty-four; he was posthumously granted Grand Guardian, enshrined in the Shrine of Worthies, and given the posthumous name Wenduan.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，御製懷舊詩，列五閣臣中。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year the emperor composed a nostalgic poem, ranking him among five grand secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: In 1779 the emperor's nostalgic poem ranked him among five leading grand secretaries.

sentences.zh: 來保能知人。

translations.literal: Lai Bao was able to recognize talent in others.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Bao had a gift for recognizing talent.

sentences.zh: 舒赫德官烏里雅蘇台將軍，疏請徙阿睦爾撒納眷屬於邊。

translations.literal: Shuhede, holding the post of Uliastai general, memorialized requesting that Amursana's dependents be moved to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Shuhede, as Uliastai general, proposed moving Amursana's dependents to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 上以其傷遠人心，震怒，遣使封刀斬之。

translations.literal: The emperor, considering this harmful to winning distant hearts, was furious and sent an envoy with a sealed sword to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, deeming this would alienate distant peoples, was furious and sent an envoy bearing a sealed sword to execute him.

sentences.zh: 來保爭甚力，以為才可大用。

translations.literal: Lai Bao argued strenuously, holding that his talent could be put to great use.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Bao argued forcefully that Shuhede's talent was too valuable to lose.

sentences.zh: 上亦悔，第曰：「已降旨！」

translations.literal: The emperor also regretted it, but only said: "The edict has already been issued!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also regretted it but said only: "The edict has already gone out!"

sentences.zh: 來保曰：「即上有恩命，臣子成麟善騎，遣追前使還。」

translations.literal: Lai Bao said: "Even if Your Majesty grants mercy, the subject Cheng Lin is skilled at riding; send him to overtake the earlier envoy and bring him back."
translations.idiomatic: Lai Bao said: "Even if Your Majesty grants mercy, Cheng Lin is an excellent rider—send him to overtake the earlier envoy and bring him back."

sentences.zh: 上允之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 歸召成麟，使齎詔追前使還。

translations.literal: On returning he summoned Cheng Lin and had him carry the edict to overtake the earlier envoy and bring him back.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he summoned Cheng Lin and sent him with the edict to overtake the earlier envoy.

sentences.zh: 成麟日夜馳三百餘裡，先前使三日到，舒赫德賴以免。

translations.literal: Cheng Lin rode day and night more than three hundred li and arrived three days before the earlier envoy; Shuhede was spared by this.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Lin rode day and night over three hundred li and arrived three days ahead of the executioner; Shuhede was thus spared.

sentences.zh: 來保善相馬，上嘗為相馬歌賜之。

translations.literal: Lai Bao was skilled at judging horses, and the emperor once composed a horse-judging song and bestowed it on him.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Bao was skilled at judging horses; the emperor once composed a horse-judging song and bestowed it on him.

sentences.zh: 劉綸，字蜰涵，江蘇武進人。

translations.literal: Liu Lun, style name Weihan, was a native of Wujin in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Lun, whose style name was Weihan, came from Wujin in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 少俊穎，六歲，能綴文，長工為古文辭。

translations.literal: As a youth he was brilliant; at six he could compose literary pieces, and when grown he excelled at classical prose.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was brilliant; at six he could compose essays, and as an adult he excelled at classical prose.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，以廩生舉博學鴻詞，試第一，授編修。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong, as a government student he was nominated for the erudition examination, placed first, and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In 1736, nominated from the government school for the erudition examination, he placed first and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 預修世宗實錄，遷侍講，進太常寺少卿。

translations.literal: He took part in compiling the Veritable Records of Emperor Shizong, was promoted to expositor, and advanced to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He helped compile the Veritable Records of the Yongzheng Emperor, rose to expositor, and became vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 四遷，擢內閣學士。

translations.literal: After four promotions he was advanced to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After four promotions he was made grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 十二年，扈蹕木蘭，奏秋郊大獵、哨鹿二賦，稱旨。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he accompanied the imperial procession to Mulan and presented two rhapsodies on the autumn hunt at the suburbs and whistle-hunting, which pleased the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1747 he accompanied the emperor to Mulan and presented rhapsodies on the autumn hunt and whistle-hunting that pleased the throne.

sentences.zh: 十四年，直南書房，授禮部侍郎，調工部。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he served in the Southern Study, was appointed vice minister of rites, and transferred to the ministry of works.
translations.idiomatic: In 1749 he served in the Southern Study, was made vice minister of rites, then transferred to the ministry of works.

sentences.zh: 十五年，命軍機處行走。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was ordered to serve in the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: In 1750 he was assigned to the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 十六年，土默特貝子哈木噶巴雅斯朗圖不按原議年限驅種地流民，命綸偕侍讀學士麒麟保往勘。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year the Tumed prince Hamigabayaslangtu did not drive off tenant farmers on seed land according to the originally agreed term; Lun was ordered, together with reader-in-waiting Qilinbao, to go and investigate.
translations.idiomatic: In 1751 the Tumed prince Hamigabayaslangtu failed to remove tenant farmers from seed land within the agreed term; Liu Lun was sent with reader-in-waiting Qilinbao to investigate.

sentences.zh: 六月，疏言：「出口民價典旗地，應遵原議三年、五年限外撤還原主。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he memorialized: "Commoners who mortgage banner land beyond the pass should, beyond the originally agreed limits of three and five years, withdraw and return it to the original owner.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he reported: "Han commoners who mortgaged banner land beyond the pass should return it after the agreed three- or five-year limits.

sentences.zh: 其領地耕種為佃戶，受僱力作為傭工，皆浮寄謀生，初無佔地意，應許力耕餬口。

translations.literal: Those who farmed on banner estates as tenants or were hired as laborers were all sojourners seeking livelihood and had no intent to occupy land from the start; they should be allowed to work the fields for subsistence.
translations.idiomatic: Tenants and hired laborers on banner estates were merely sojourners seeking livelihood without intent to seize land and should be allowed to farm for subsistence.

sentences.zh: 至領地墾荒，積累辛勤，始得成熟，不同價典，年滿先還原主。

translations.literal: As for opening wasteland on banner estates, after accumulated labor it finally became fertile; this differed from mortgaged land, and when the term expired it should first be returned to the original owner.
translations.idiomatic: Land opened on banner estates through years of labor differed from mortgaged plots and should revert to the owner when terms expired.

sentences.zh: 所需自種地有贏，仍給種以償前勞。

translations.literal: If self-cultivated land yielded a surplus, seed should still be given to compensate prior labor.
translations.idiomatic: If self-cultivated surplus remained, seed grain should compensate prior labor.

sentences.zh: 木頭城、三座塔居人稠密，許照常居住。

translations.literal: Mutoucheng and Santa were densely settled; residents were permitted to remain as before.
translations.idiomatic: The densely settled areas of Mutoucheng and Santa were permitted to remain inhabited as before.

sentences.zh: 設三座塔巡檢一，資彈壓。」

translations.literal: One Santa inspector was established to assist in keeping order."
translations.idiomatic: A Santa inspector was appointed to maintain order."

sentences.zh: 詔從其議。

translations.literal: An edict approved his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his recommendations.

sentences.zh: 父憂歸。

translations.literal: He returned home on his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 服闋，十八年，除戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, in the eighteenth year he was appointed vice minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning, in 1753 he was appointed vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 十九年，兼順天府尹。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was given concurrent charge as Shuntian metropolitan magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: In 1754 he was given concurrent charge as Shuntian metropolitan magistrate.

sentences.zh: 故事，順天府公牘，治中、通判不署名。

translations.literal: By precedent, on Shuntian official documents the assistant prefect and vice prefect did not sign their names.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent Shuntian documents did not bear the assistant prefect's or vice prefect's signatures.

sentences.zh: 綸請以錢穀屬治中，獄訟屬通判，先署牘呈尹可否之。

translations.literal: Lun requested that grain taxes be assigned to the assistant prefect and lawsuits to the vice prefect, who would first sign documents and present them to the magistrate for approval or rejection.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Lun proposed assigning grain taxes to the assistant prefect and lawsuits to the vice prefect, who would sign drafts for the magistrate's approval.

sentences.zh: 大軍西征準噶爾，師行，役車供偫，壹切辦治無誤。

translations.literal: When the great army marched west against Dzungaria, as the troops moved he supplied carts and provisions for transport, arranging everything without error.
translations.idiomatic: When the army marched west against Dzungaria, he supplied transport and provisions without a hitch.

sentences.zh: 二十年，準噶爾平，予獎敘。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year Dzungaria was pacified and he received commendation for merit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1755, after the pacification of Dzungaria, he received a merit commendation.

sentences.zh: 浙江按察使富勒渾劾巡撫鄂樂舜授意布政使同德勒派商銀，命綸如浙江偕兩江總督尹繼善等會訊。

translations.literal: Zhejiang surveillance commissioner Fulehun impeached Governor Eleshun for instructing Provincial Treasurer Tongdele to levy merchant silver; Lun was ordered to go to Zhejiang and join Liangjiang Governor-General Yin Jishan and others in joint investigation.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhejiang surveillance commissioner Fulehun impeached Governor Eleshun for instructing Provincial Treasurer Tongdele to levy merchant silver, Liu Lun was sent to Zhejiang to investigate jointly with Liangjiang Governor-General Yin Jishan and others.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，覆奏鄂樂舜受銀屬實，擬絞候；

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year they reported back that Eleshun's acceptance of silver was substantiated and proposed deferred strangulation;
translations.idiomatic: In 1756 they reported Eleshun's taking of silver substantiated and proposed deferred strangulation;

sentences.zh: 同德未知情；

translations.literal: Tongde was unaware;
translations.idiomatic: Tongdele was found unaware of the scheme;

sentences.zh: 富勒渾誣劾，擬杖流。

translations.literal: Fulehun's impeachment was false and he was proposed for beating and exile.
translations.idiomatic: Fulehun's impeachment was deemed false and he was proposed for beating and exile.

sentences.zh: 上以富勒渾參款已實，不應議罪，責綸等失當。

translations.literal: The emperor held that since Fulehun's charges were substantiated, he should not be put on trial for an offense, and rebuked Lun and others for impropriety.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held Fulehun's charges substantiated and should not be punished, rebuking Liu Lun and others for error.

sentences.zh: 部議奪官，有旨從寬留任，罷直軍機處。

translations.literal: The ministry proposed stripping him of office; an edict showed leniency and retained him in post, but removed him from service in the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry proposed stripping his office; the emperor showed leniency and kept him in post but removed him from the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，命仍入直。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was ordered to resume service in the council.
translations.idiomatic: In 1757 he was ordered back to the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 二十四年六月，奏薊州、寶坻等縣蝻子萌動，州縣官事繁，督捕未能周遍，飭千總、外委同佐雜分捕，參將偕監司巡察勤惰，報可。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the twenty-fourth year he memorialized that locust nymphs were hatching in Jizhou, Baodi, and other counties; district and county officials had heavy duties and could not supervise capture comprehensively; he ordered company commanders and external deputies together with assistant officials to divide capture duties, and regional commanders together with surveillance officials to inspect diligence and slackness; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of 1759 he reported locust nymphs hatching in Jizhou and Baodi; with county officials overburdened, he ordered company commanders and deputies to divide capture duties and regional commanders with surveillance officials to inspect diligence; the plan was approved.

sentences.zh: 進左都御史。

translations.literal: He was advanced to left censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，偕侍郎伊祿順赴西安勘將軍嵩阿禮剋兵糧、勒餽送等款，得實，論如律。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, together with Vice Minister Yilushun, he went to Xi'an to investigate General Song'a for embezzling military grain, extorting gifts, and other charges; the facts were established and he was sentenced according to law.
translations.idiomatic: In 1760, with Vice Minister Yilushun, he investigated Xi'an General Song'a for embezzling military grain and extorting gifts; the charges were proved and Song'a was sentenced by law.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，進兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was advanced to minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: In 1761 he was promoted to minister of war.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，調戶部，協辦大學士，加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was transferred to the ministry of revenue, made associate grand secretary, and given the additional title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In 1763 he was transferred to the ministry of revenue, made associate grand secretary, and given the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 三十年，母憂歸。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he returned home on his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: In 1765 he returned home to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 甫除喪，詔起吏部尚書，仍協辦大學士。

translations.literal: Just as mourning ended, an edict recalled him as minister of personnel, still as associate grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Just as mourning ended, an edict recalled him as minister of personnel and associate grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，授文淵閣大學士，兼工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year he was appointed grand secretary of the Hall of Literary Depths and given concurrent charge as minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: In 1771 he was appointed grand secretary of the Hall of Literary Depths with concurrent charge as minister of works.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，卒，命皇子臨其喪，贈太子太傅，祀賢良祠，諡文定。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year he died; princes were ordered to attend his funeral; he was posthumously granted Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, enshrined in the Shrine of Worthies, and given the posthumous name Wending.
translations.idiomatic: In 1773 he died; princes were ordered to attend his funeral; he was posthumously granted Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, enshrined in the Shrine of Worthies, and given the posthumous name Wending.

sentences.zh: 綸性至孝，親喪三年不御酒肉。

translations.literal: Lun was supremely filial; during his parents' mourning he abstained from wine and meat for three years.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Lun was deeply filial, abstaining from wine and meat throughout the three-year mourning period.

sentences.zh: 直軍機處十年，與大學士劉統勳同輔政，有「南劉東劉」之稱。

translations.literal: He served in the Grand Council for ten years and assisted in government together with Grand Secretary Liu Tongxun, gaining the designation "the southern Liu and the eastern Liu."
translations.idiomatic: After ten years on the Grand Council assisting government alongside Grand Secretary Liu Tongxun, they were known as "the southern Liu and the eastern Liu."

sentences.zh: 器度端凝，不見有喜慍色。

translations.literal: His bearing was dignified and steady, and joy or anger never showed on his face.
translations.idiomatic: His bearing was dignified and steady, and neither joy nor anger ever showed on his face.

sentences.zh: 出入殿門，進止有恆處。

translations.literal: Entering and leaving the palace hall, his comings and goings always had fixed places.
translations.idiomatic: When entering and leaving the palace hall, he always took the same fixed route.

sentences.zh: 自工部侍郎歸，買宅數楹。

translations.literal: After returning from his post as vice minister of works, he bought a residence of several bays.
translations.idiomatic: When he retired from the vice ministership of works, he bought a modest house of a few bays.

sentences.zh: 後服官二十年，未嘗益一椽半甓。

translations.literal: Later, through twenty years of holding office, he never added a single rafter or half a tile.
translations.idiomatic: Over the next twenty years in office he never added so much as a rafter or half a tile.

sentences.zh: 衣履垢敝不改作，朝必盛服，曰：「不敢褻朝章也！」

translations.literal: His clothes and shoes were worn and soiled yet he did not have them remade; for court he always wore full dress, saying: "I dare not slight the court insignia!"
translations.idiomatic: Though his clothes and shoes were worn and soiled, he would not have them replaced; for court he always wore full dress, saying, "I dare not slight the insignia of office!"

sentences.zh: 侍郎王昶充軍機處章京，嘗嚴冬有急奏具草，夜半詣綸，綸起燃燭，操筆點定。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Wang Chang served as a clerk of the Grand Council; once in deep winter there was an urgent memorial draft ready, and at midnight he called on Lun; Lun rose, lit a candle, took up his brush, and corrected and finalized it.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Wang Chang, serving as a Grand Council clerk, once brought an urgent memorial draft on a bitter winter night; Liu Lun rose at midnight, lit a candle, and edited it with his brush.

sentences.zh: 寒甚，呼家人具酒脯，而廚傳已空，僅得白棗十數枚侑酒。

translations.literal: The cold was severe; he called for the household to prepare wine and dried meat, but the kitchen stores were empty, and he had only a dozen or so white jujubes to accompany the wine.
translations.idiomatic: It was bitterly cold, and he asked his household for wine and dried meat, but the larder was bare—he could offer only a dozen white jujubes to go with the wine.

sentences.zh: 其清儉類此。

translations.literal: His purity and frugality were of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His austerity and frugality were typical of this sort.

sentences.zh: 校士尤矜慎，嘗曰：「衡文始難在取，繼難在去。

translations.literal: In examining candidates he was especially strict and careful, and once said: "In evaluating essays the first difficulty lies in selecting, the next in rejecting.
translations.idiomatic: In examining candidates he was especially strict and careful, and once said, "Evaluating examination essays is hard first in choosing whom to pass, and harder still in choosing whom to fail.

sentences.zh: 文佳劣相近​​，一去取間於我甚易，獨不為士子計乎？」

translations.literal: When essays are close in quality between good and poor, to pass or fail them is very easy for me—should I alone not consider the candidates?"
translations.idiomatic: When essays differ only slightly in quality, passing or failing them is easy for the examiner—but should one not consider what that means for the candidates?"

sentences.zh: 較量分寸，輒至夜分不伴奏倦。

translations.literal: Weighing every fine distinction, he would often work until midnight without showing weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Weighing every fine distinction, he often worked until midnight without showing fatigue.

sentences.zh: 文法六朝，根柢漢、魏；

translations.literal: In prose he followed the style of the Six Dynasties, with roots in the Han and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In prose he modeled himself on the Six Dynasties, with foundations in the Han and Wei.

sentences.zh: 於詩喜明高啟，謂能入唐人門閾。

translations.literal: In poetry he favored Gao Qi of the Ming, saying that he could enter the threshold of Tang poets.
translations.idiomatic: In poetry he admired the Ming poet Gao Qi, holding that he had crossed the threshold into Tang-level mastery.

sentences.zh: 子躍雲，字服先。

translations.literal: His son was Yueyun, style name Fuxian.
translations.idiomatic: His son Liu Yueyun, whose style name was Fuxian.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十一年進士及第，授編修。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year of Qianlong he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In 1766 he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed a Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 累遷禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to vice minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 六十年，充會試副考官，以校閱失當下吏議，左遷奉天府府丞，罷歸。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year he served as associate chief examiner of the metropolitan examination; for improper review he was referred to the officials for deliberation, demoted to assistant prefect of Fengtian Prefecture, and dismissed to return home.
translations.idiomatic: In 1795 he served as associate chief examiner of the metropolitan examination; for improper grading he was referred for investigation, demoted to assistant prefect of Fengtian Prefecture, and sent home.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年，召為大理寺少卿，遷工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing he was summoned as vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review and promoted to vice minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: In 1799 he was recalled as vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review and soon promoted to vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 上御門，躍雲誤班未至，左遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: When the emperor held court at the gate, Yueyun missed his rank and failed to arrive; he was demoted to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor held gate audience, Liu Yueyun was absent from his proper place in the ranks and was demoted to grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 复授兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was again appointed vice minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: He was later reappointed vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 休致，卒。

translations.literal: He retired and died.
translations.idiomatic: He retired from office and died.

sentences.zh: 殿試例糊名，躍雲對策，高宗親置上第，喜曰：「此劉綸子，不意朕竟得之！」

translations.literal: The palace examination customarily used sealed names; Yueyun answered the policy questions, and Gaozong personally placed him in the top tier, saying with pleasure: "This is Liu Lun's son—I did not expect that I should obtain him!"
translations.idiomatic: Palace examination papers were normally submitted under sealed names; when Liu Yueyun answered the policy questions, the Qianlong Emperor personally ranked him at the top and said with delight, "This is Liu Lun's son—I never expected I would get him!"

sentences.zh: 及視學江西，有清名。

translations.literal: When he served as provincial education commissioner in Jiangxi, he had a reputation for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: As provincial education commissioner in Jiangxi, he earned a reputation for integrity.

sentences.zh: 高宗意鄉用，以忤和珅，主會試，坐浮言，黜。

translations.literal: Gaozong intended to appoint him to local service, but because he offended Heshen, when he chaired the metropolitan examination he was dismissed on a charge of loose talk.
translations.idiomatic: The Qianlong Emperor had intended to appoint him to provincial service, but after he offended Heshen and chaired the metropolitan examination, he was dismissed on a charge of spreading rumors.

sentences.zh: 仁宗召起，老矣，終不竟其用。

translations.literal: Jiaqing recalled him to office, but he was already old and in the end his talents were never fully employed.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiaqing Emperor recalled him to office, but he was already old and never fully used again.

sentences.zh: 子逢祿，見儒林傳。

translations.literal: His son Fenglu is treated in the Biographies of Scholars.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fenglu is recorded in the Biographies of Scholars.

sentences.zh: 劉統勳，字延清，山東諸城人。

translations.literal: Liu Tongxun, style name Yanqing, was a native of Zhucheng in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tongxun, whose style name was Yanqing, came from Zhucheng in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 父棨，官四川布政使。

translations.literal: His father Qi held the post of financial commissioner of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qi served as financial commissioner of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 統勳，雍正二年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: Tongxun passed the examinations in the second year of Yongzheng, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tongxun earned his jinshi degree in 1724, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 先後直南書房、上書房，四遷至詹事。

translations.literal: He successively served in the Southern Study and the Upper Study, and after four promotions reached the post of tutor to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively in the Southern Study and Upper Study and, after four promotions, became tutor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，擢內閣學士。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong he was promoted to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In 1736 he was promoted to grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 命從大學士嵇曾筠赴浙江學習海塘工程。

translations.literal: He was ordered to follow Grand Secretary Ji Zengyun to Zhejiang to study sea-dike engineering.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to accompany Grand Secretary Ji Zengyun to Zhejiang to study sea-dike construction.

sentences.zh: 二年，授刑部侍郎，留浙江。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed vice minister of justice and remained in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1737 he was appointed vice minister of justice and remained in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 三年，還朝。

translations.literal: In the third year he returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: In 1738 he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 四年，母憂歸。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he returned home on account of his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In 1739 he returned home to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 六年，授刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed vice minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: In 1741 he was appointed vice minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 服闋，詣京師。

translations.literal: When mourning was completed, he went to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning period ended, he proceeded to the capital.

sentences.zh: 擢左都御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to censor-in-chief of the left.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「大學士張廷玉歷事三朝，遭逢極盛，然晚節當慎，責備恆多。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Grand Secretary Zhang Tingyu has served through three reigns and met with the utmost prosperity, yet in his later years he should be cautious, for criticism is often directed at him.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Grand Secretary Zhang Tingyu has served three reigns at the height of imperial favor, yet in his later years he should be cautious, for criticism of him is frequent.

sentences.zh: 竊聞輿論，動雲'張、姚二姓佔半部縉紳'，張氏登仕版者，有張廷璐等十九人，姚氏與張氏世婚，仕宦者姚孔鋹等十人。

translations.literal: I have privately heard public opinion constantly saying that 'the Zhang and Yao surnames occupy half the gentry of the ministry'; among those of the Zhang clan entered on the roster of office are Zhang Tinglu and eighteen others, and the Yao clan, intermarried with the Zhangs for generations, has ten in official service, including Yao Kongqiang.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard it said that 'the Zhang and Yao clans occupy half the ministry's gentry ranks'; nineteen Zhangs hold office, including Zhang Tinglu, and ten Yaos, intermarried with the Zhangs for generations, including Yao Kongqiang.

sentences.zh: 二姓本桐城巨族，其得官或自科目薦舉，或起襲廕議敘，日增月益。

translations.literal: Both clans were originally great families of Tongcheng; their obtaining office came either through the examination system and recommendation, or through inheritance of privilege and deliberative appointment, increasing day by day and month by month.
translations.idiomatic: Both were great Tongcheng clans whose members entered office through examinations, recommendations, or inherited privilege, their numbers growing steadily.

sentences.zh: 今未能遽議裁汰，惟稍抑其遷除之路，使之戒滿引嫌，即所以保全而造就之也。

translations.literal: At present one cannot abruptly propose elimination, but only slightly restrain their path of promotion and transfer, causing them to guard against complacency and withdraw when propriety requires—this is precisely the way to preserve and cultivate them.
translations.idiomatic: They cannot be abruptly purged, but restraining their promotions would teach them restraint and withdrawal when propriety demands it—and thus preserve and cultivate them.

sentences.zh: 請自今三年內，非特旨擢用，概停升轉。」

translations.literal: I request that from now for three years, except by special edict, all promotions and transfers be generally suspended."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that for the next three years, except by special edict, all their promotions and transfers be suspended."

sentences.zh: 又言：「尚書公訥親年未強仕，綜理吏、戶兩部。
