translations.literal: He also said: "Minister Ne Qin is not yet in the prime of life, yet he supervises both the ministries of personnel and revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Minister Ne Qin is still young, yet he supervises both the ministries of personnel and revenue.

sentences.zh: 典宿衛，贊中樞，兼以出納王言，時蒙召對。

translations.literal: He presides over the palace guard, assists the central administration, and also transmits and receives imperial words, frequently being summoned for audience.
translations.idiomatic: He oversees the palace guard, assists the central administration, transmits imperial instructions, and is frequently summoned for private audience.

sentences.zh: 屬官奔走恐後，同僚亦爭避其鋒。

translations.literal: Subordinate officials rushed in fear of falling behind, and colleagues also competed to avoid his sharp edge.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates scrambled to obey him, and colleagues competed to avoid crossing him.

sentences.zh: 部中議覆事件，或輾轉駁詰，或過目不留，出一言而勢在必行，定一稿而限逾積日，殆非懷謙集益之道。

translations.literal: In the ministry, matters for deliberation and reply were sometimes sent back and forth in repeated rejection and questioning, or passed over without retention; one word from him and it had to be carried out, one draft fixed and deadlines exceeded by accumulated days—this was scarcely the way of humble receptivity and gathering benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Ministry business was sometimes sent back repeatedly for revision or dismissed without review; a single word from him became mandatory, and deadlines piled up—hardly the way of humble consultation and collective judgment.

sentences.zh: 請加訓示，俾知省改。

translations.literal: I request that instruction be added so that he may know to reflect and reform.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that he be admonished so that he may reflect and reform.

sentences.zh: 其所司事，或量行裁減，免曠廢之虞。」

translations.literal: The affairs under his charge might, as appropriate, be reduced in measure, to avoid the worry of neglect through overextension."
translations.idiomatic: Some of his responsibilities might be reduced as appropriate, lest overextension lead to neglect."

sentences.zh: 兩疏入，上諭曰：「朕思張廷玉、訥親若果擅作威福，劉統勳必不敢為此奏。

translations.literal: When both memorials were submitted, the emperor instructed: "I consider that if Zhang Tingyu and Ne Qin truly abused power for personal ends, Liu Tongxun would certainly not dare to submit these memorials.
translations.idiomatic: When both memorials arrived, the emperor said: "If Zhang Tingyu and Ne Qin truly abused their power, Liu Tongxun would never have dared submit these memorials.

sentences.zh: 今既有此奏，則二臣並無聲勢能箝制僚寀可知，此國家之祥也。

translations.literal: Now that these memorials exist, it is clear that neither minister had such influence as to suppress the officials—this is an auspicious sign for the state.
translations.idiomatic: That these memorials were submitted shows neither minister could suppress his colleagues—a good sign for the state.

sentences.zh: 大臣任大責重，原不能免人指摘。

translations.literal: Great ministers bear heavy responsibility and originally cannot escape people's criticism.
translations.idiomatic: Great ministers bear heavy burdens and cannot escape criticism.

sentences.zh: 聞過則喜，古人所尚。

translations.literal: To rejoice on hearing of one's faults is what the ancients honored.
translations.idiomatic: Rejoicing when one's faults are pointed out is what the ancients valued.

sentences.zh: 若有幾微芥蒂於胸臆間，則非大臣之度矣。

translations.literal: If the slightest grudge lodges in the breast, that is not the measure of a great minister.
translations.idiomatic: If the slightest resentment lodges in one's heart, one lacks the measure of a great minister.

sentences.zh: 大學士張廷玉親族甚眾，因而登仕籍者亦多。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Zhang Tingyu has very many kinsmen, and many have accordingly entered the registers of office.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Zhang Tingyu has a large extended family, and many kinsmen hold office.

sentences.zh: 今一經察議，人知謹飭，轉於廷玉有益。

translations.literal: Now, once this scrutiny and discussion has occurred, people will know to be careful and restrained, which in turn will benefit Tingyu.
translations.idiomatic: Now that this scrutiny has occurred, people will know to be careful— which will benefit Zhang Tingyu.

sentences.zh: 訥親為尚書，固不當模棱推諉，但治事或有未協，朕時加教誨，誡令毋自滿足。

translations.literal: Ne Qin as minister certainly should not be evasive and shirk responsibility, but in handling affairs there may be points not in accord; I constantly add instruction and admonition, warning him not to be self-satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: Ne Qin as minister should not be evasive, but if his handling of affairs falls short, I constantly instruct and warn him against self-satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 今見此奏，益當自勉。

translations.literal: Now, seeing this memorial, he should all the more exert himself.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing this memorial, he should redouble his efforts.

sentences.zh: 至職掌太多，如有可減，侯朕裁定。」

translations.literal: As for having too many duties, if any can be reduced, await my decision."
translations.idiomatic: If any of his duties can be reduced, I shall decide."

sentences.zh: 尋命以統勳疏宣示廷臣。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he ordered Tongxun's memorial to be displayed to the court officials.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor soon ordered Liu Tongxun's memorial read to the court.

sentences.zh: 命勘海塘。

translations.literal: He was ordered to inspect the sea dikes.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to inspect the sea dikes.

sentences.zh: 十一年，署漕運總督。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he served as acting director-general of grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: In 1746 he served as acting director-general of grain transport.

sentences.zh: 還京。

translations.literal: He returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 十三年，命同大學士高斌按山東賑務，並勘河道。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was ordered, together with Grand Secretary Gao Bin, to investigate Shandong relief affairs and also inspect the river works.
translations.idiomatic: In 1748 he was ordered, with Grand Secretary Gao Bin, to oversee Shandong famine relief and inspect river works.

sentences.zh: 時運河盛漲，統勳請濬聊城引河，分運河水注海。

translations.literal: At the time the Grand Canal was in full flood; Tongxun requested dredging the Liaocheng diversion channel to divide the canal water and pour it into the sea.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Canal was then at flood stage; Liu Tongxun proposed dredging the Liaocheng diversion channel to split canal water toward the sea.

sentences.zh: 德州哨馬營、東平戴村二壩，皆改令低，沂州江楓口二壩，俟秋後培高，俾水有所洩。

translations.literal: The two dams at Shaomaying in Dezhou and Daicun in Dongping were all ordered lowered; the two dams at Jiangfengkou in Yizhou were to be raised after autumn, so that water would have an outlet.
translations.idiomatic: The dams at Shaomaying in Dezhou and Daicun in Dongping were lowered; those at Jiangfengkou in Yizhou were to be raised after autumn so water could drain.

sentences.zh: 遷工部尚書，兼翰林院掌院學士，改刑部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to minister of works, concurrently chief academician of the Hanlin Academy, then changed to minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was made minister of works and chief Hanlin academician, then transferred to minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 十七年，命軍機處行走。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was ordered to serve in the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: In 1752 he was assigned to the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 十八年，以江南邵伯湖減水二閘及高郵車邏壩決，命偕署尚書策楞​​往按。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, because the two sluice gates for reducing water at Shaobo Lake in Jiangnan and the Che'er dam in Gaoyou burst, he was ordered to go together with Acting Minister Celen to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: In 1753, after sluice gates at Shaobo Lake and the Che'er dam in Gaoyou burst, he was sent with Acting Minister Celen to investigate.

sentences.zh: 合疏言河員虧帑誤工，詔奪河督高斌、協辦河務巡撫張師載職，窮治侵帑諸吏。

translations.literal: Together they memorialized that river officials had embezzled funds and delayed the work; an edict stripped River Director Gao Bin and Zhang Shizai, the governor assisting river affairs, of their posts and thoroughly prosecuted the officials who had embezzled funds.
translations.idiomatic: They jointly reported that river officials had embezzled funds and botched the work; the emperor stripped River Director Gao Bin and assisting governor Zhang Shizai of their posts and prosecuted the embezzlers.

sentences.zh: 九月，銅山小店汛河決，統勳疏論同知李焞、守備張賓呈報稽誤。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the river burst at the Xiaodian station in Tongshan; Tongxun memorialized criticizing Sub-Prefect Li Chun and Garrison Commander Zhang Bin for delay in reporting.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the river burst at Xiaodian station in Tongshan; Liu Tongxun reported that Sub-Prefect Li Chun and Garrison Commander Zhang Bin had delayed their reports.

sentences.zh: 上以焞、賓平日侵帑，聞且窮治，自知罪重，河漲任其衝決，立命誅之，並縶斌、師載令視行刑。

translations.literal: The emperor, considering that Chun and Bin had ordinarily embezzled funds and, hearing that prosecution was imminent, knew their guilt was grave and let the river flood break through unchecked, immediately ordered them executed and also bound Bin and Shizai to witness the execution.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, knowing Li Chun and Zhang Bin had long embezzled funds and, hearing prosecution was imminent, had let the flood break through unchecked, immediately ordered their execution and bound Gao Bin and Zhang Shizai to witness it.

sentences.zh: 統勳駐銅山督塞河，十二月，工成。

translations.literal: Tongxun remained at Tongshan to supervise blocking the river; in the twelfth month the work was completed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tongxun remained at Tongshan to supervise the repair; the work was completed in the twelfth month.

sentences.zh: 統勳偕策楞疏陳稽察工料諸事，詔如所議行。

translations.literal: Tongxun, together with Celen, memorialized setting forth matters of auditing labor and materials; an edict ordered implementation as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tongxun and Celen reported on auditing labor and materials; the emperor approved their proposals.

sentences.zh: 大學士陳世倌疏言黃河入海，套櫃增多，致壅塞，命統勳往勘。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Chen Shigu memorialized that as the Yellow River entered the sea, sediment bars had increased and caused blockage; Tongxun was ordered to go and inspect.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Chen Shigu reported that sediment bars at the Yellow River's mouth were causing blockage; Liu Tongxun was ordered to investigate.

sentences.zh: 統勳疏言：「海口舊在雲梯關，今海退河淤，增長百餘裡，櫃套均在七曲港上，河流無所阻遏。」

translations.literal: Tongxun memorialized: "The river mouth was formerly at Yuntiguan; now the sea has receded and the river silted up, extending more than a hundred li; the sediment bars are all above Qiqu Harbor, and the river flow is nowhere obstructed."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tongxun reported: "The river mouth was once at Yuntiguan; the sea has since receded and the river silted up over a hundred li; sediment bars lie above Qiqu Harbor, and the current is unobstructed."

sentences.zh: 上又命清察江南河工未結諸案，統勳疏言未結款一百一十一萬有奇，請定限核報。

translations.literal: The emperor also ordered a clearing investigation of unsettled cases in Jiangnan river works; Tongxun memorialized that unsettled funds amounted to more than 1.11 million and requested a fixed deadline for audit and report.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also ordered an audit of unsettled Jiangnan river-work accounts; Liu Tongxun reported over 1.11 million taels outstanding and asked for a deadline to settle them.

sentences.zh: 又以河道總督顧琮請於祥符、滎澤諸縣建壩，並濬引河，命統勳往勘。

translations.literal: Also, because River Director Gu Zong requested building dams in Xiangfu, Xingze, and other counties and dredging diversion channels, Tongxun was ordered to go and inspect.
translations.idiomatic: When River Director Gu Zong proposed building dams in Xiangfu, Xingze, and other counties and dredging diversion channels, Liu Tongxun was sent to inspect.

sentences.zh: 統勳議擇地培堤壩，引河上無來源，中經沙地，易淤墊，當罷，上從之。

translations.literal: Tongxun judged that choosing a site to build embankments and dams was acceptable, but the diversion channel had no upstream source, passed through sandy ground, and was easily silted up—it should be abandoned; the emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tongxun approved building embankments and dams but rejected the diversion channel, which had no upstream source and would silt up in sandy terrain; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 十九年，加太子太傅。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was granted the title of Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In 1754 he was granted the title of Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 五月，命協辦陝甘總督，賜孔雀翎。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he was ordered to assist the governor-general of Shaanxi and Gansu and was granted a peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he was assigned to assist the governor-general of Shaanxi-Gansu and was granted a peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 時方用兵準噶爾，統勳請自神木至巴里坤設站一百二十五，並裁度易馬、運糧諸事，命如所議速行。

translations.literal: At the time troops were being deployed against the Dzungars; Tongxun requested establishing one hundred twenty-five stations from Shenmu to Barkol and also adjudicating matters of horse exchange and grain transport; he was ordered to carry out the proposals swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: With war underway against the Dzungars, Liu Tongxun proposed establishing 125 relay stations from Shenmu to Barkol and arranging horse exchange and grain transport; the emperor ordered immediate implementation.

sentences.zh: 二十年，廷議駐兵巴里坤、哈密，命察勘。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year the court debated stationing troops at Barkol and Hami; he was ordered to inspect and survey.
translations.idiomatic: In 1755 the court debated garrisoning Barkol and Hami; Liu Tongxun was ordered to survey the sites.

sentences.zh: 統勳至巴里坤，阿睦爾撒納叛，攻伊犁，伊犁將軍班第死事，未得報。

translations.literal: When Tongxun reached Barkol, Amursana rebelled and attacked Ili; Ili General Ban Di died in the line of duty, but the report had not yet arrived.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Tongxun reached Barkol, Amursana rebelled and attacked Ili; Ili General Ban Di had died in battle, though the news had not yet arrived.

sentences.zh: 定西將軍永常自木壘引師退，統勳疏請還守哈密。

translations.literal: Dingxi General Yongchang withdrew his army from Mori; Tongxun memorialized requesting to return and hold Hami.
translations.idiomatic: Dingxi General Yongchang withdrew his army from Mori; Liu Tongxun memorialized proposing to fall back and hold Hami.

sentences.zh: 上責其附和永常，置班第於不問，命並永常奪職，逮治。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked him for echoing Yongchang and leaving Ban Di unaddressed, and ordered both Yongchang and him stripped of office and arrested for trial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked him for echoing Yongchang and ignoring Ban Di's fate, stripped both men of office, and ordered their arrest.

sentences.zh: 其子墉亦奪職，與在京諸子皆下刑部獄，籍其家。

translations.literal: His son Yong was also stripped of office; together with his other sons in the capital they were all sent to the prison of the ministry of justice, and his household was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: His son Liu Yong was also stripped of office; all his sons in the capital were imprisoned in the ministry of justice, and the family property was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 旋上怒解，諭：「統勳所司者糧餉馬駝，軍行進止，將軍責也。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the emperor's anger eased, and he instructed: "What Tongxun was charged with was grain, pay, horses, and camels; the advance and halt of the army was the general's responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's anger soon eased, and he said: "Liu Tongxun was responsible for grain, pay, horses, and camels; troop movements were the general's responsibility.

sentences.zh: 設令模棱之人緘默不言，轉可不至獲罪。

translations.literal: Had an equivocal man kept silent and said nothing, he might instead have escaped guilt.
translations.idiomatic: An equivocal man who kept silent might never have been punished.

sentences.zh: 是其言雖謬，心尚可原。

translations.literal: Thus although his words were mistaken, his heart may still be forgiven.
translations.idiomatic: Though his advice was wrong, his motives may be forgiven.

sentences.zh: 永常尚不知死綏，何怪於統勳？

translations.literal: Yongchang still did not know of dying in defense of the post—how can Tongxun be blamed?
translations.idiomatic: Yongchang did not yet know Ban Di had died defending his post—how could Liu Tongxun be blamed?

sentences.zh: 統勳在漢大臣中尚奮往任事，從寬免罪，發往軍營交班第等令治軍需贖罪。」

translations.literal: Among Han ministers Tongxun still showed boldness in undertaking affairs; he was leniently exempted from guilt and sent to the army camp to be handed over to Ban Di and others to manage military supplies in atonement."
translations.idiomatic: Among Han ministers Liu Tongxun still showed bold initiative; he was leniently pardoned and sent to the army camp under Ban Di and others to manage military supplies in atonement."

sentences.zh: 釋其諸子。

translations.literal: His sons were all released.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were released.

sentences.zh: 二十一年六月，授刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the twenty-first year he was appointed minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of 1756 he was appointed minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 尋命勘銅山縣孫家集漫工，解總河富勒赫任，即命統勳暫攝。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was ordered to inspect the flood-control work at Sunjiaji in Tongshan County; Director-General of the Grand Canal Fulehe was relieved of his post, and Tongxun was immediately ordered to serve temporarily in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to inspect flood-control work at Sunjiaji in Tongshan County; Grand Canal Director Fulehe was dismissed and Liu Tongxun was appointed acting director-general.

sentences.zh: 是冬，工竟。

translations.literal: That winter the work was completed.
translations.idiomatic: The work was completed that winter.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，命赴徐州督修近城石壩，加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was ordered to go to Xuzhou to supervise repair of the stone dam near the city and was granted the title of Senior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In 1757 he was ordered to Xuzhou to supervise repair of the city stone dam and was granted the title of Senior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，調吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was transferred to minister of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In 1758 he was transferred to minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，命協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was ordered to assist as grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In 1759 he was appointed assistant grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，拜東閣大學士，兼管禮部、兵部。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was appointed grand secretary of the Eastern Pavilion with concurrent charge of the ministries of rites and war.
translations.idiomatic: In 1761 he was made grand secretary of the Eastern Pavilion with concurrent charge of the ministries of rites and war.

sentences.zh: 八月，偕協辦大學士兆惠查勘河南楊橋漫工。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, together with Assistant Grand Secretary Zhaohui, he inspected the flood-control work at Yangqiao in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he joined Assistant Grand Secretary Zhaohui in inspecting flood-control work at Yangqiao in Henan.

sentences.zh: 十二月，工竟。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the work was completed.
translations.idiomatic: The project was finished in the twelfth month.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，上南巡，復命偕兆惠勘高、寶河湖入江路，疏請開引河，擇地築閘壩。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, when the emperor made a southern tour, he again ordered him together with Zhaohui to survey the route by which the Gao and Bao rivers entered the Yangtze, and in a memorial requested opening a diversion channel and selecting a site to build sluice gates and dams.
translations.idiomatic: In year 27, during the emperor's southern tour, he was again ordered to join Zhaohui in surveying how the Gao and Bao rivers flow into the Yangtze route. They memorialized requesting the excavation of a diversion channel and the construction of sluice gates and dams at a suitable site.

sentences.zh: 上諭謂：「所議甚合朕意。」

translations.literal: The emperor instructed, saying: "What was proposed accords very well with my intent."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Your proposal matches my thinking perfectly."

sentences.zh: 又以直隸景州被水，命勘德州運河，疏請移吏董理四女寺、哨馬營兩引河，毋使淤閼。

translations.literal: He also, because Jing Prefecture in Zhili had suffered flooding, ordered a survey of the Grand Canal at Dezhou, and in a memorial requested assigning officials to oversee the two diversion channels at Sinüsi and Shaomaying, lest they silt up and become blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Because Jing Prefecture in Zhili had been inundated, he was also ordered to inspect the Grand Canal at Dezhou and memorialized that officials be reassigned to manage the Sinüsi and Shaomaying diversion channels, so they would not silt shut.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，充上書房總師傅，兼管刑部，教習庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, he was appointed Chief Tutor of the Upper Study, concurrently supervised the Ministry of Punishments, and instructed Hanlin probationers.
translations.idiomatic: In year 28 he became Chief Tutor of the Upper Study, concurrently headed the Ministry of Punishments, and tutored Hanlin probationers.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，命往江南酌定清口疏濬事宜。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year, he was ordered to go to Jiangnan to determine arrangements for dredging at Qingkou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 33 he was sent to Jiangnan to settle plans for dredging at Qingkou.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，复勘疏運河。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year, he again surveyed and dredged the Grand Canal.
translations.idiomatic: In year 34 he conducted another survey and dredging of the Grand Canal.

sentences.zh: 三十八年十一月，卒。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year, eleventh month, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eleventh month of year 38.

sentences.zh: 是日夜漏盡，入朝，至東華門外，輿微側，啟帷則已瞑。

translations.literal: That night, when the night watch had ended, he entered court; reaching outside the East Flowery Gate, his sedan tilted slightly; when the curtain was drawn open, he had already closed his eyes in death.
translations.idiomatic: That very night, after the final watch, he set out for court. Outside the East Flowery Gate his sedan tilted slightly; when attendants lifted the curtain, he was already dead.

sentences.zh: 上聞，遣尚書福隆安齎藥馳視，已無及。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, he dispatched Minister Fu Long'an to bring medicine and hurry to look in on him, but it was already too late.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing this, the emperor sent Minister Fu Long'an with medicine posthaste, but it was too late.

sentences.zh: 贈太傅，祀賢良祠，諡文正。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Tutor, enshrined in the Shrine of Worthy Officials, and given the posthumous name Wenzheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Tutor, honored in the Shrine of Worthy Officials, and given the posthumous title Wenzheng ("Upright in Letters").

sentences.zh: 上臨其喪，見其儉素，為之慟。

translations.literal: The emperor attended his funeral; seeing how frugal and plain it was, he grieved for him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor attended the funeral and, struck by its austerity, wept for him.

sentences.zh: 回蹕至乾清門，流涕謂諸臣曰：「朕失一股肱！」

translations.literal: Returning to the Forbidden City and reaching the Gate of Heavenly Purity, with tears flowing he said to the officials: "I have lost an arm and a leg!"
translations.idiomatic: On returning through the Gate of Heavenly Purity, he wept and told his ministers, "I have lost one of my chief supports!"

sentences.zh: 既而曰：「如統勳乃不愧真宰相。」

translations.literal: After a moment he said: "Only one like Tongxun can deserve to be called a true prime minister."
translations.idiomatic: Then he added, "Only someone like Tongxun truly deserves the name of prime minister."

sentences.zh: 統勳歲出按事，如廣東按糧驛道明福違禁折收，如雲南按總督恆文、巡撫郭一裕假上貢抑屬吏賤值巿金，如山西按布政使蔣洲抑屬吏補虧帑，如陝西按西安將軍都賚侵餉，如歸化城按將軍保德等侵帑，如蘇州按布政使蘇崇阿誤論書吏侵帑，如江西按巡撫阿思哈受賕，皆論如律。

translations.literal: Each year when Tongxun went out on inspection, he prosecuted cases according to law: in Guangdong he investigated grain transport courier director Ming Fu for forbidden discount collection; in Yunnan, Governor-General Heng Wen and Governor Guo Yiyu for using tribute pretexts to coerce subordinates into selling gold at low prices; in Shanxi, Provincial Administration Commissioner Jiang Zhou for coercing subordinates to make up treasury shortfalls; in Shaanxi, Xi'an General Du Lai for embezzling military pay; at Guihuacheng, General Baode and others for embezzling treasury funds; in Suzhou, Provincial Administration Commissioner Su Chong'a for wrongly convicting clerks of embezzlement; in Jiangxi, Governor Asiha for taking bribes—all were judged according to law.
translations.idiomatic: On his annual inspection tours, Tongxun prosecuted every case to the letter of the law: in Guangdong, grain transport courier director Ming Fu for unlawful discount collections; in Yunnan, Governor-General Heng Wen and Governor Guo Yiyu for using imperial tribute as a pretext to force subordinates to sell gold cheaply; in Shanxi, Provincial Administration Commissioner Jiang Zhou for extorting subordinates to cover treasury deficits; in Shaanxi, Xi'an General Du Lai for seizing military stipends; at Guihuacheng, General Baode and others for treasury embezzlement; in Suzhou, Provincial Administration Commissioner Su Chong'a for wrongfully convicting clerks of embezzlement; in Jiangxi, Governor Asiha for bribery—all were punished according to law.

sentences.zh: 其視楊橋漫工也，河吏以芻茭不給為辭，月餘事未集。

translations.literal: When he inspected the Yang Bridge embankment work, river officials used the excuse that fodder was not supplied, and for more than a month the matter was not completed.
translations.idiomatic: While overseeing the Yang Bridge levee project, river officials claimed for over a month that they lacked fodder, and the work remained unfinished.

sentences.zh: 統勳微行，見大小車載芻茭凡數百輛，皆弛裝困臥。

translations.literal: Tongxun went about in plain dress; he saw large and small carts loaded with fodder numbering several hundred, all with harnesses loosened while drivers lay exhausted asleep.
translations.idiomatic: Dressing as a commoner, Tongxun found hundreds of carts laden with fodder, their drivers sleeping off their exhaustion with harnesses slack.

sentences.zh: 有泣者，問之，則主者索賄未遂，置而不收也。

translations.literal: There was one weeping; asking him, it turned out the person in charge had demanded a bribe without success and had set the load aside without accepting it.
translations.idiomatic: One driver was weeping. Asked why, he said the receiving officer had demanded a bribe, and when it was not paid, refused to accept the load.

sentences.zh: 即令縛主者至，數其罪，將斬之。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered the person in charge bound and brought forth, enumerated his crimes, and was about to behead him.
translations.idiomatic: Tongxun had the officer bound, listed his crimes, and was ready to execute him.

sentences.zh: 巡撫以下為固請，乃杖而荷校以徇，薪芻一夕收立盡。

translations.literal: The governor and those below earnestly pleaded; then he was caned and made to wear the cangue as a public warning, and fodder was collected and finished in a single night.
translations.idiomatic: The governor and others pleaded desperately, so Tongxun had the man beaten and paraded in the cangue instead; all the fodder was accepted and cleared overnight.

sentences.zh: 踰月工遂竟。

translations.literal: After a month the work was then completed.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month the project was finished.

sentences.zh: 方金川用兵，統勳屢議撤兵，及木果木軍覆，上方駐熱河，統勳留京治事，天暑甚，以兼上書房總師傅，檢視諸皇子日課。

translations.literal: While troops were being deployed in Jinchuan, Tongxun repeatedly proposed withdrawing the army; when the army was destroyed at Mugemu, the emperor was then staying at Rehe; Tongxun remained in the capital to manage affairs; the weather was very hot; because he concurrently served as Chief Tutor of the Upper Study, he inspected the daily lessons of the princes.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jinchuan campaign Tongxun had repeatedly urged withdrawal. When the army was wiped out at Mugemu, the emperor was at Rehe while Tongxun remained in Beijing to govern. In the sweltering heat, while also serving as Chief Tutor of the Upper Study, he inspected the princes' daily coursework.

sentences.zh: 廷寄急召，比入對，上曰：「昨軍報至，木果木軍覆，溫福死綏。

translations.literal: An urgent summons came by palace courier; when he entered audience, the emperor said: "Yesterday the military report arrived—the army was destroyed at Mugemu, and Wen Fu died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: An urgent palace summons arrived. When Tongxun came before the emperor, the emperor said, "Yesterday's dispatch reported the army destroyed at Mugemu and Wen Fu killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 朕煩懣無計，用兵乎，抑撤兵乎？」

translations.literal: I am vexed and at my wits' end—shall we continue the war, or withdraw the troops?"
translations.idiomatic: I am anguished and see no way forward—do we fight on, or pull back?"

sentences.zh: 統勳對曰：「日前兵可撤，今則斷不可撤。」

translations.literal: Tongxun replied: "Previously the troops could have been withdrawn; now they absolutely cannot be withdrawn."
translations.idiomatic: Tongxun answered, "Before, withdrawal might have been possible; now it is absolutely out of the question."

sentences.zh: 復問誰可任者，統勳頓首曰：「臣料阿桂必能了此事。」

translations.literal: He again asked who could be entrusted; Tongxun kowtowed and said: "Your servant expects A Gui can certainly settle this affair."
translations.idiomatic: Asked who could take command, Tongxun kowtowed and said, "I believe A Gui is the man to finish this."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕正欲專任阿桂，特召卿決之。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I was just about to place sole responsibility on A Gui; I specially summoned you to decide it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I was already set on putting A Gui solely in charge—I summoned you especially to confirm it.

sentences.zh: 卿意與合，事必濟矣。」

translations.literal: Your view agrees with mine; the affair will surely succeed."
translations.idiomatic: Your judgment matches mine; the matter will surely succeed."

sentences.zh: 即日令還京師。

translations.literal: That same day he was ordered to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: That same day A Gui was ordered back to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 戶部疏論諸行省州縣倉庫多空缺，上欲盡罷州縣吏不職者，而以筆帖式等官代之。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue memorialized discussing how warehouses in the provinces, prefectures, and counties were largely empty and deficient; the emperor wished to dismiss entirely all incompetent county and prefectural officials and replace them with bithesi and other such officials.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue reported widespread empty granaries and treasury shortfalls across the provinces. The emperor wanted to remove all incompetent local officials and replace them with bithesi and similar functionaries.

sentences.zh: 召統勳諭意，且曰：「朕思之三日矣，汝意云何？」

translations.literal: He summoned Tongxun to convey his intent, and also said: "I have thought on this for three days; what is your view?"
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Tongxun to explain his plan and said, "I have been thinking about this for three days. What do you think?"

sentences.zh: 統勳默不言。

translations.literal: Tongxun was silent and did not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Tongxun said nothing.

sentences.zh: 上詰責，統勳徐曰：「聖聰思至三日，臣昏耄，誠不敢遽對，容退而熟審之。」

translations.literal: The emperor pressed and rebuked him; Tongxun slowly said: "Your sacred intelligence has pondered it for three days; your servant is old and muddled, and truly dares not answer hastily—allow me to withdraw and consider it carefully."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor pressed him, Tongxun replied carefully, "Your Majesty has pondered this for three days; I am old and dull and dare not answer rashly. Allow me to withdraw and think it through."

sentences.zh: 翌日入對，頓首言曰：「州縣治百姓者也，當使身為百姓者為之。」

translations.literal: The next day he entered audience and, kowtowing, said: "Prefectures and counties govern the common people; those who are themselves common people ought to govern them."
translations.idiomatic: The next day he kowtowed and said, "Prefectures and counties exist to govern the people—they should be run by men who are of the people themselves."

sentences.zh: 語未竟，上曰：「然。」

translations.literal: Before he had finished speaking, the emperor said: "So it is."
translations.idiomatic: Before he could finish, the emperor said, "Exactly."

sentences.zh: 事遂寢。

translations.literal: The matter was then dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 上為懷舊詩，列五閣臣中，稱其「神敏剛勁，終身不失其正」云。

translations.literal: The emperor composed a poem remembering old times; among the five Grand Secretaries he praised him, saying "spiritually keen and fiercely resolute, to the end of life never losing his rectitude."
translations.idiomatic: In a nostalgic poem listing the five Grand Secretaries, the emperor praised him as "keen and unyielding, never once losing his integrity to the end of his days."

sentences.zh: 子二：墉、堪。

translations.literal: He had two sons: Yong and Kan.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Yong and Kan.

sentences.zh: 墉，字崇如，乾隆十六年進士，自編修再遷侍講。

translations.literal: Yong, styled Chongru, passed the metropolitan examination in the sixteenth year of Qianlong; from Compiler he was again promoted to Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: Yong, styled Chongru, became a jinshi in Qianlong 16 and rose from Compiler to Lecturer.

sentences.zh: 二十年，統勳得罪，並奪墉官下獄，事解，賞編修，督安徽學政。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, Tongxun was found guilty; Yong's office was also stripped and he was imprisoned; when the affair was resolved, he was rewarded with the post of Compiler and made Educational Commissioner of Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: In year 20, when Tongxun fell from favor, Yong was stripped of rank and imprisoned. After the case closed he was restored as Compiler and appointed Educational Commissioner of Anhui.

sentences.zh: 疏請州縣約束貢監，責令察優劣。

translations.literal: In a memorial he requested that prefectures and counties restrain tribute students and jiansheng, and charged them to investigate merits and defects.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized urging prefectures and counties to rein in tribute students and licentiates and to inspect their conduct.

sentences.zh: 督江蘇學政，疏言府縣吏自​​瞻顧，畏刁民，畏生監，兼畏吏胥，闒冘怠玩。

translations.literal: As Educational Commissioner of Jiangsu, he memorialized that prefectural and county officials looked to their own interests, feared troublesome commoners, feared licentiates, and also feared clerks and runners, becoming lazy and negligent.
translations.idiomatic: As Jiangsu Educational Commissioner, he reported that local officials looked out only for themselves, fearing troublemakers, licentiates, and even their own clerks—growing slack and indifferent.

sentences.zh: 上嘉其知政體，飭兩江總督尹繼善等淬厲除舊習。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his understanding of government fundamentals and ordered Governor-General Yin Jishan of the Two Jiangs and others to sharpen themselves and remove old habits.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor applauded his grasp of good governance and ordered Governor-General Yin Jishan of the Two Jiangs and others to root out these entrenched habits.

sentences.zh: 授山西太原知府，擢冀寧道。

translations.literal: He was appointed Prefect of Taiyuan in Shanxi and promoted to Circuit Intendant of Jining.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Prefect of Taiyuan, Shanxi, then promoted to Circuit Intendant of Jining.

sentences.zh: 以官知府時失察僚屬侵帑，發軍台效力。

translations.literal: Because while serving as prefect he failed to detect subordinates' embezzlement of treasury funds, he was sent to the military courier stations to perform penal labor.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as prefect he failed to detect subordinates' embezzlement and was sentenced to penal service on the military courier route.

sentences.zh: 逾年釋還，命在修書處行走。

translations.literal: After a year he was released and returned; he was ordered to serve in the book-compilation office.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was released and assigned to the imperial book-compilation office.

sentences.zh: 旋推統勳恩，命仍以知府用，授江蘇江寧知府，有清名。

translations.literal: Soon, by extending Tongxun's grace, he was ordered still to be used as a prefect; he was appointed Prefect of Jiangning in Jiangsu and had a reputation for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, through his father's credit, he was restored as a prefect and appointed to Jiangning in Jiangsu, where he earned a name for probity.

sentences.zh: 再遷陝西按察使。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Provincial Surveillance Commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to Provincial Surveillance Commissioner of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，服闋，授內閣學士，直南書房。

translations.literal: Upon completing mourning for his father, he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat and served in the Southern Study.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his father, he became a Grand Secretariat Academician and served in the Southern Study.

sentences.zh: 遷戶部、吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of the Ministries of Revenue and Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Minister of Revenue and Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 授湖南巡撫，遷左都御史，仍直南書房。

translations.literal: He was appointed Governor of Hunan, transferred to Censor-in-Chief of the Left, and still served in the Southern Study.
translations.idiomatic: He became Governor of Hunan, then Censor-in-Chief of the Left, continuing to serve in the Southern Study.

sentences.zh: 命偕尚書和珅如山東按巡撫國泰貪縱狀，得實，授工部尚書，充上書房總師傅。

translations.literal: He was ordered together with Minister Heshen to go to Shandong and investigate Governor Guotai's greedy and unrestrained conduct; the facts were established; he was appointed Minister of Works and appointed Chief Tutor of the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered with Minister Heshen to Shandong to investigate Governor Guotai's corruption and excess, the charges were confirmed. He was then made Minister of Works and Chief Tutor of the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 署直隸總督，授協辦大學士。

translations.literal: He acted as Governor-General of Zhili and was appointed Associate Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting Governor-General of Zhili and was made Associate Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 五十四年，以諸皇子師傅久不入書房，降為侍郎銜。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year, because as tutor to the princes he had long failed to enter the study, he was demoted to Vice Minister rank.
translations.idiomatic: In year 54 he was demoted to Vice Minister rank for long neglecting his duties as the princes' tutor in the study.

sentences.zh: 尋授內閣學士，三遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat; after three promotions he became Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon restored as a Grand Secretariat Academician and later thrice promoted to Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶二年，授體仁閣大學士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiaqing, he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Body-and-Benevolence Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 2 he became Grand Secretary of the Tiren Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 命偕尚書慶桂如山東讞獄，並按行河決，疏請寬濬下游。

translations.literal: He was ordered together with Minister Qing Gui to go to Shandong to review criminal cases, and also to inspect river breaches along the way; in a memorial he requested dredging the lower reaches more broadly.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent with Minister Qing Gui to Shandong to review cases and inspect river breaches, memorializing for broader dredging downstream.

sentences.zh: 四年，加太子少保。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was granted Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 疏陳漕政，僉丁不慎，途中盜米，致有鑿舟自沉，或鬻及檣舵，舟存而不可用，請飭各行省僉丁宜求殷實，皆如所議行。

translations.literal: In a memorial he set forth grain transport policy: hired laborers were not careful, grain was stolen en route, leading to cases of boring holes in boats to sink them, or selling even masts and rudders so boats remained but were unusable; he requested that all provinces in hiring laborers should seek solid and substantial men—all was carried out as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on grain transport: careless hired boatmen stole grain along the route, sometimes scuttling boats or selling off masts and rudders until vessels survived but could not sail. He urged provinces to hire only reliable men—all measures were adopted.

sentences.zh: 九年，卒，年八十五，贈太子太保，祀賢良祠，諡文清。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he died, aged eighty-five; he was posthumously granted Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, enshrined in the Shrine of Worthy Officials, and given the posthumous name Wenqing.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year 9 at eighty-five, posthumously honored as Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, enshrined in the Shrine of Worthy Officials, and given the posthumous title Wenqing ("Pure in Letters").

sentences.zh: 墉工書，有名於時。

translations.literal: Yong was skilled at calligraphy and had fame in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was an accomplished calligrapher renowned in his day.

sentences.zh: 鐶之，統勳次子堪之子也。

translations.literal: Huanzhi was the son of Kan, Tongxun's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Huanzhi was the son of Kan, Tongxun's second son.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十四年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the metropolitan examination in the forty-fourth year of Qianlong.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in Qianlong 44.

sentences.zh: 自檢討累遷至戶部尚書，兼領順天府府尹。

translations.literal: From Proofreader he was promoted in succession to Minister of Revenue, concurrently heading the Prefect of Shuntian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Rising from Proofreader, he eventually became Minister of Revenue while also serving as Prefect of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶二十二年，上自熱河還京師，鐶之入見。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Jiaqing, when the emperor returned from Rehe to the capital, Huanzhi entered audience.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 22, when the emperor returned from Rehe to Beijing, Huanzhi was summoned to audience.

sentences.zh: 上以順天府奏事稀、捕教匪不時得詰，鐶之不能對，但言方旱災不敢急捕賊。

translations.literal: Because the Shuntian Prefecture memorials were sparse and bandits of the teaching faith were not captured in timely fashion and could be questioned, the emperor questioned Huanzhi; he could not answer, but only said that there was presently drought disaster and he dared not urgently capture bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pressed him on Shuntian's infrequent reports and failure to catch White Lotus rebels promptly. Huanzhi had no answer, pleading only that drought made aggressive policing imprudent.

sentences.zh: 上又問賑災當設粥廠幾所、需米若干，鐶之又不能對。

translations.literal: The emperor again asked how many congee kitchens should be set up for famine relief and how much rice would be needed; Huanzhi again could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Asked how many relief kitchens were needed and how much rice they would require, Huanzhi again had nothing to say.

sentences.zh: 上降旨責其玩愒，命以侍郎候補。

translations.literal: The emperor issued an edict rebuking his negligence and ordered him to serve as Vice Minister on reserve appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked his negligence and demoted him to reserve Vice Minister rank.

sentences.zh: 复累遷吏部尚書，加太子少保。

translations.literal: Later he was again promoted in succession to Minister of Personnel and granted Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was later reinstated and rose again to Minister of Personnel, with the rank of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，卒，諡文恭。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang, he died; he was given the posthumous name Wengong.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Daoguang 1 and was posthumously titled Wengong ("Respectful in Letters").

sentences.zh: 論曰：明內閣主旨擬，承旨撰敕，其在唐、宋，特知制誥之職。

translations.literal: The commentary says: The Ming Grand Secretariat mainly drafted rescripts and received edicts to compose imperial decrees; in the Tang and Song, this was merely the office of drafting edicts and proclamations.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: The Ming Grand Secretariat chiefly drafted rescripts and composed edicts on imperial order—roles that in Tang and Song amounted to little more than drafters of proclamations.

sentences.zh: 以王命所出入，密勿獻替，遂號為宰相。

translations.literal: Because the king's commands passed through them and in confidential proximity they offered corrections and replacements, they came to be called prime ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Because imperial commands flowed through them and they offered confidential counsel at the sovereign's side, they came to be styled prime ministers.

sentences.zh: 軍機處制與相類。

translations.literal: The Grand Council's system was similar.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Council operated along similar lines.

sentences.zh: 世謂大學士非兼軍機處，不得為真宰相。

translations.literal: The world says that a Grand Secretary who does not concurrently serve in the Grand Council cannot be a true prime minister.
translations.idiomatic: It was commonly held that a Grand Secretary who did not also serve in the Grand Council was no true prime minister.

sentences.zh: 勝此任者，非以其慎密，則以其通敏。

translations.literal: Those who excel in this appointment rely either on discretion and secrecy, or on comprehensive quickness.
translations.idiomatic: Men who excelled in this office did so either through discretion or through quick-wittedness.

sentences.zh: 慎密則不洩，通敏則不滯，不滯不洩，樞機之責盡矣。

translations.literal: Discretion and secrecy then there is no leakage; comprehensive quickness then there is no stagnation; without stagnation and without leakage, the responsibilities of the pivot mechanism are fully fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: Discretion prevented leaks; quick-wittedness prevented bottlenecks. Where there was neither delay nor disclosure, the duties of the pivot were fully met.

sentences.zh: 本，世宗舊臣，由敦、來保、綸、統勳次第入直。

translations.literal: In this chapter—Yongzheng's old ministers—You Dun, Laibao, Lun, and Tongxun entered service in the inner offices in succession.
translations.idiomatic: This section treats Yongzheng's veteran ministers: You Dun, Laibao, Lun, and Tongxun, who entered imperial service in turn.

sentences.zh: 由敦左遷而未罷直，統勳罷而復入，尤以決疑定計見契於高宗，許為有古大臣風，亮哉！

translations.literal: You Dun was demoted to the left but was not removed from inner service; Tongxun was dismissed but re-entered; especially by resolving doubts and fixing plans he found accord with Emperor Gaozong, praised as having the manner of the great ministers of antiquity—how clear!
translations.idiomatic: You Dun was demoted yet kept his place in the inner circle; Tongxun was dismissed but returned. Above all, Tongxun won Emperor Gaozong's trust by resolving doubts and fixing strategy—a man said to bear the air of the great ministers of old. Admirable indeed!
